data.title: Show HN: Somo – a human friendly alternative to netstat
data.author: hollow64
data.article_summary: Somo是一款用于Linux系统上监控socket和端口的工具，作为netstat的更人性化替代品。它具有直观的表格视图，支持多种过滤选项，并能够交互式地终止进程。安装方式有通过Debian的.deb包或使用cargo进行安装，运行时通常需要sudo权限。Somo提供多种过滤标志，如按协议、端口、IP、程序、PID等进行筛选，还支持结合过滤和终止进程操作。该工具旨在简化网络连接和端口的管理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对工具（特别是`netstat`和`ss`）的使用体验、功能需求以及平台兼容性的讨论。

不同观点：
• [ale42] 认为表格模式（或水平线）在终端中占用太多空间，询问是否有选项可以禁用。他关注的是界面布局和显示效率，特别是在有多个连接时。

• [neiesc] 提供了在Arch系统上通过AUR安装相关软件包的链接，似乎是在回应如何获取或使用该工具，但没有直接回答ale42的问题。

• [nubb] 表达了对`netstat`的强烈习惯依赖，提到自己经常使用`netstat -pna`，并暗示不愿意改用其他工具。

• [kreetx] 指出`ss`是`netstat`的现代替代品，虽然常用命令参数相同，但在某些方面并没有显著改进。这暗示了`ss`在功能上可能更先进，但并没有完全取代`netstat`的必要性。

• [mrweasel] 对`ss`持积极态度，认为它能满足其90%的使用需求，并解决了记忆`netstat`参数的问题。这表明部分用户认为新工具更加便捷。

• [at0mic22] 提到`ss`不能在Mac OS上使用，因为procfs不支持。这指出了平台兼容性的问题，限制了该工具在某些操作系统上的使用。

补充讨论：
• 用户对工具的使用习惯各不相同，有的用户对传统工具（如`netstat`）有很强的依赖性，而另一些用户则对新工具（如`ss`）持欢迎态度。
• 平台兼容性是用户选择工具时需要考虑的一个重要因素，特别是在跨平台使用时。
• 界面布局和显示效率也是部分用户关心的问题，尤其是在处理大量连接时。

A human-friendly alternative to netstat for socket and port monitoring on Linux.
✨ Features:
pleasing to the eye thanks to a nice table-view
filterable (see filter-options below)
interactive killing of processes
from
netstat -tulpn
to
somo -l
(almost half the characters, can you believe it?)
⬇️ Installation:
Option 1 - Debian:
If you use a Debian OS go to
releases
and download the latest .deb release.
Option 2 - From crates.io:
cargo install somo
Most of the time you will want to run this in
sudo
mode to see all processes and ports. By default, this is not possible when installed via cargo. But you can create a symlink so the binary can be run as root:
sudo ln -s
~
/.cargo/bin/somo /usr/local/bin/somo
sudo somo
#
this works now
🏃‍♀️ Running somo:
To run somo just type:
sudo somo
Filtering:
You can use the following flags to filter based on different attributes:
filter flag
description
value
--proto
filter by either TCP or UDP
tcp
or
udp
--port, -p
filter by a local port
port number, e.g
5433
--remote-port
filter by a remote port
port number, e.g
443
--ip
filter by a remote IP
IP address e.g
0.0.0.0
--program
filter by a client program
program name e.g
chrome
--pid, -p
filter by a PID
PID number, e.g
10000
--open, -o
filter by open connections
-
--listen, -l
filter by open connections
-
--exclude-ipv6
don't list IPv6 connections
-
Process killing:
With the
--kill, -k
flag you can choose to kill a process after inspecting the connections using an interactive selection option.
You can of course also apply filters and the kill-flag at the same time:
somo --program postgres -k

data.title: Container: Apple's Linux-Container Runtime
data.author: jzelinskie
data.article_summary: "container" 是一个由苹果开发的工具，用于在Mac上创建和运行基于轻量级虚拟机的Linux容器。该工具使用Swift编写，针对Apple Silicon进行了优化。它支持OCI标准的容器镜像，允许从任何标准容器注册表拉取和运行镜像，并可将构建的镜像推送回注册表。使用前需在Apple Silicon Mac上运行，并依赖macOS 26 Beta 1的新功能，虽然也能在macOS 15上运行，但可能存在网络限制问题。安装和卸载可通过脚本完成，项目文档提供了详细的使用指南和贡献方式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Apple 的新容器化工具及其相关技术实现和应用场景

不同观点：
• slroger 认为该工具只需要一个图形用户界面（GUI）就能接近完美，强调了用户体验的改进需求。
• dang 提到相关讨论线程，指出虽然有些讨论主题相似，但存在显著且微妙的差异，特别是关于容器化和不同框架的实现。
• jzelinskie 解释了该工具如何通过创建轻量级虚拟机来运行兼容 OCI（Docker）的容器，并提供了相关技术细节和资源链接。
• 90s_dev 讨论了 Swift 作为 Rust 替代方案的可行性，提出了对 Swift API 命名方式的质疑。
• gardaani 分享了使用 lima 在 macOS 上运行 Linux 虚拟机的经验，并考虑用 Apple 的新工具替代 lima。
• sverhagen 质疑工具命名方式的合理性，担心是否能够被商标化。
• zarazas 关注该工具是否能与 Docker 集成，以提高 Mac 上 Docker 容器的性能。
• wmf 建议将讨论合并到另一个相关主题中。
• punnerud 询问该工具是否能支持在 iOS 和 macOS 上下载的 AppStore 应用旁运行容器。
• spockz 深入探讨了该工具与 Firecracker 等其他虚拟化技术的比较，关注性能和使用体验，并提出了对 Apple Silicon 特性的利用问题。
• rcarmo 对该工具不支持 iPadOS 表示遗憾。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了多个相关技术，如容器化、虚拟化框架、Swift 框架、Docker 和 Podman 等，显示了社区对这些技术实现细节的高度关注。
• 争议的焦点包括工具命名是否合理、Swift API 的命名方式、以及该工具与现有解决方案的性能对比。
• 社区对该工具在不同 Apple 操作系统（macOS、iOS、iPadOS）上的应用前景有不同看法，特别是对 iPadOS 的支持缺失表示失望。

通过这些讨论，可以看出社区对 Apple 新容器化工具的技术实现、性能优化、应用场景和命名等方面有广泛关注和不同见解。

container
container
is a tool that you can use to create and run Linux containers as lightweight virtual machines on your Mac. It's written in Swift, and optimized for Apple silicon.
The tool consumes and produces OCI-compliant container images, so you can pull and run images from any standard container registry. You can push images that you build to those registries as well, and run the images in any other OCI-compliant application.
container
uses the
Containerization
Swift package for low level container, image, and process management.
Get started
Requirements
You need an Apple silicon Mac to run
container
. To build it, see the
BUILDING
document.
container
relies on the new features and enhancements present in the macOS 26 Beta 1. You can run the tool on macOS 15, but the
container
maintainers typically will not address issues discovered on macOS 15 that cannot be reproduced on the macOS 26 Beta 1.
There are
significant networking limitations
that impact the usability of
container
on macOS 15.
Install or upgrade
If you're upgrading, first uninstall your existing
container
while preserving your user data:
uninstall-container.sh -k
Download the latest signed installer package for
container
from the
GitHub release page
.
To install the tool, double click the package file and follow the instructions. Enter your administrator password when prompted, to give the installer permission to place the installed files under
/usr/local
.
Uninstall
Use the
uninstall-container.sh
script to remove
container
from your system. To remove your user data along with the tool, run:
uninstall-container.sh -d
To retain your user data so that it is available should you reinstall later, run:
uninstall-container.sh -k
Next steps

a guided tour of
container
by building, running, and publishing a simple web server image.
Learn how to
use various
container
features
.

technical overview
of
container
.

API documentation
.
Contributing
Contributions to
container
are welcomed and encouraged. Please see our
main contributing guide
for more information.

A tool for creating and running Linux containers using lightweight virtual machines on a Mac. It's written in Swift, and optimized for Apple silicon.

data.title: Implementing DOES> in Forth, the entire reason I started this mess
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要讨论了在Forth编程语言中实现`DOES>`功能的过程和挑战。作者首先提到自己对`DOES>`的实现感到困惑，因为它不像其他功能那样直观。通过一个具体例子，作者解释了`STAR`和`.ROW`两个词的用途，并详细介绍了`SHAPE`和`CREATE`的功能。`CREATE`用于在Forth字典中创建新词，而`DOES>`则用于修改新词的行为，使其不仅将主体地址压入堆栈，还执行其后代码。文章还提到，实现`DOES>`需要考虑三个时间点：编译时、新词定义时和执行时，并指出这一功能在不同CPU架构和Forth实现中的复杂性。最终，作者通过研究和实验成功实现了`DOES>`，并简化了其在6809架构和ITC实现中的解释。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Forth编程语言中的CREATE和DOES>的实现、使用及其相关争议，以及Forth中的数据结构性能问题。

不同观点：
• **throwaway81523**：解释了CREATE和DOES>的执行语义和工作原理。CREATE在字典中创建一个词，并将其地址压入堆栈，而DOES>则覆盖默认的执行行为。他指出这种设计在早期Forth中通过<BUILDS ... DOES>实现，后来为了优化和标准化改为了CREATE ... DOES>。然而，这种优化在现代微控制器的闪存环境中可能不理想，因此在某些MCU实现（如FlashForth）中又恢复了<BUILDS ... DOES>的使用。

• **zelphirkalt**：关注Forth的栈结构和数据结构性能问题。他质疑在栈结构下如何实现高效的数据结构，因为线性访问时间可能导致性能问题。但他知道Forth中有高效的数据结构实现，只是不理解其原理。

• **jackdoe**：表达了对DOES>的个人挫折感，认为实现DOES>很困难，但承认问题可能在于自己的经验不足。尽管如此，他还是觉得CREATE DOES>可能需要被新的构造取代，但目前仍会使用CREATE DOES>。

• **mikewarot**：表示自己曾编写过Forth，但仍然不理解DOES>的具体作用，带有一些调侃意味。

• **rwmj**：指出Jonesforth没有实现DOES>，因为它复杂且不是理解Forth基础所必需的。同时表示自己很好地解决了这一问题。

• **5-**：提到colorForth中通过颜色来精化阶段概念，可能与DOES>有关，但希望有更 knowledgeable 的人参与讨论。

• **pyinstallwoes**：直接询问DOES>的实际意义和好处，并惊讶于很少有公开的Forth实现使用它。

补充讨论：
• **rickcarlino**：提供了一个关于RetroForth中类似概念的参考，表达了对Forth内部机制深入探讨的欣赏。

争议焦点：
• DOES>的实现复杂性和必要性是讨论中的一个争议点。有人认为它复杂且不易实现，但也有人承认其重要性和正确性。

• Forth中栈结构与数据结构性能之间的关系也是讨论的一个重点，有人质疑其性能实现方式。

44231594.article_content:
The Boston Diaries
The ongoing saga of a programmer who doesn't live in Boston, nor does he even like Boston, but yet named his weblog/journal “The Boston Diaries.”
Go figure.
Monday, June 09, 2025
Implementing DOES> in Forth, the entire reason I started this mess
The issue
I had with
DOES>
isn't that it's hard to use—it's just that I had no idea how one would go about implementing it,
much like Javascript programmers use closures without having to think about how they're implemented
(even if they're aware of closures in the first place).
So,
before going into how it works,
a sample from
Starting Forth
is in order.
: STAR 42 EMIT ;
: .ROW CR 8 0 DO
DUP 128 AND IF STAR ELSE SPACE THEN 2*
LOOP DROP ;
: SHAPE CREATE 8 0 DO C, LOOP
DOES> DUP 7 + DO I C@ .ROW -1 +LOOP CR ;
HEX 18 18 3C 5A 99 24 24 24 SHAPE MAN
These two words support the example.
The first word,
STAR
just prints a asterisk
(42 is the ASCII code for the word).
The second word,
.ROW
,
takes an 8-bit value and for each bit,
if it's a 1,
prints an asterisk,
otherwise,
it prints a space.
DO
LOOP
is Forth's
for
loop by the way.
The next word,
SHAPE
is the interesting one.
But first,
we need to discuss
CREATE
.
This word creates a new entry in the Forth dictionary by reading the next word
(defined as a collection of non-space letters)
in the input as the name.
It then gives the newly created word a default action of pushing the address of the body of the word into the stack.
Going ahead a bit,
the word
MAN
just after
CREATE
is run will look like this
(in assembly):
man		fdb	shape	; link to next word
fdb	.xt - .name
.name		fcc	'man'
.xt		fdb	forth_core_create.runtime
.body
When
MAN
is run,
the address of
.body
will be pushed onto the stack.
CREATE
is typically used to create “smart data structures”—data structures that know how to do some action.
Now,
getting back to the example,
when
SHAPE
is run,
the first thing it does is call
CREATE
to create a new word,
then it compiles 8 values off the top of the stack into the body of the newly created word.
Just prior to
DOES>
,
MAN
will look like:
man		fdb	shape	; link to next word
fdb	.xt - .name
.name		fcc	'man'
.xt		fdb	forth_core_create.runtime
.body		fcb	$24
fcb	$24
fcb	$24
fcb	$99
fcb	$5A
fcb	$3C
fcb	$18
fcb	$18
Now we get to
DOES>
.
Due to the nature of what it does,
DOES>
is an immediate word—that is,
its executing during compilation to do the voodoo that it do.
Um, does.
Somehow,
it needs to modify the newly created word to not only push the address of its body onto the stack,
but execute the code that appears after itself.
So the code to be executed needs to be compiled and stored somewhere,
and somehow
MAN
(in this example) needs to run this code.
And this was the problem I had with the word—
how does this all work?
Even the well known
JonesForth
,
implemented as an
ITC
,
didn't bother with implementing
DOES>
(and now that I have implemented
DOES>
,
I suspect I know why JonesForth didn't implement it).
The runtime portion of
CREATE
just pushes the address of the body of the word into the stack.
The data bytes following the
xt
have no meaning in and of themselves
(even as code it's nonsensical).
I did a search and found only
one page
that describes how to implement
DOES>
,
but:
it was part three of a series of articles describing how Forth's are implemented;
using terminology no longer used by the ANS Forth standard;
attempting to describe how to implement Forth on several different
CPU
architectures;
using a few different methods (like
ITC
,
DTC
and
STC
);
and on this page, a wierd side trip through another Forth word
;CODE
.
It wasn't an exactly easy source to read,
but between part three and
part one
,
I was able to puzzle it out
(and it makes much more sense now that I've done it).
Now I can discribe the result using a single architecture
(6809) and a single implementation (
ITC
).
The trick here is to realize that
DOES>
has a temporal aspect unlike any other Forth word.
Most immediate words in Forth have two temporal aspects—at the time of compilation,
and later at runtime.
For instance,
IF
's compile time aspect is to compile a conditional jump into the word,
and the runtime aspect is to do said conditional jump
(at least,
it does so in my implementation).
But
DOES>
has
three
temporal aspects:
: SHAPE CREATE ...a DOES> ( time 1 ) ...b ;
...c SHAPE MAN (time 2 )
MAN (time 3 )
At time 1,
we are compiling a word that creates other words
(so at this point,
CREATE
is compiled, not run).
The compiler looks up
DOES>
,
notices that it's an immediate word and executes it.
DOES>
at this point needs to include code to cause
SHAPE
to stop executing,
then somehow leave … something … behind for time 2,
and somehow compile the rest of the code
...b
for later execution.
At time 2,
we're defining a new word.
CREATE
has been called and the initialization code for this new word
…a
has been executed.
At this point,
DOES>
needs to modify the new word … somehow … to execute the code that followed it at time 1.

44231594.article_summary: 这篇文章主要讨论了在Forth编程语言中实现`DOES>`功能的过程和挑战。作者首先提到自己对`DOES>`的实现感到困惑，因为它不像其他功能那样直观。通过一个具体例子，作者解释了`STAR`和`.ROW`两个词的用途，并详细介绍了`SHAPE`和`CREATE`的功能。`CREATE`用于在Forth字典中创建新词，而`DOES>`则用于修改新词的行为，使其不仅将主体地址压入堆栈，还执行其后代码。文章还提到，实现`DOES>`需要考虑三个时间点：编译时、新词定义时和执行时，并指出这一功能在不同CPU架构和Forth实现中的复杂性。最终，作者通过研究和实验成功实现了`DOES>`，并简化了其在6809架构和ITC实现中的解释。

data.article_summary: **patolette** 是一个 C / Python 颜色量化与抖动库，核心实现了基于加权变体的 Xiaolin Wu 的 PCA 色彩量化器。主要特性包括：避免轴对齐分割、支持 CIEL*u*v* 和 ICtCp 色彩空间、可选的显著图支持以突出视觉重点、可选的 KMeans 优化。该库尚未完善，不建议用于生产环境，但已具备一定可用性。目前没有 PyPI 包，需手动安装。对于 x86 架构，支持通过 CMAKE_ARGS 设置指令集优化（如 AVX512）。提供了在 Linux、macOS 和 Windows 上的安装步骤，但 Windows 下构建较为复杂，建议参考说明。

patolette
is a
C / Python
color quantization and dithering library.
At its core, it implements a weighted variant of Xiaolin Wu's PCA-based quantizer (not to be confused with the popular one from
Graphics Gems vol. II
, which is already available
here
).
Some of its key features are:
Avoids axis-aligned subdivisions
Supports the
CIEL*u*v*
and
ICtCp
color spaces
Optional use of saliency maps to give higher weight to areas that stand out visually
Optional
KMeans
refinement
The library is still in need of a ton of improvements and most definitely not ready for production use, but it's already very useable.
Installation
A
PyPI
package is not yet available. Until then, installation is manual but it should hopefully be painless 🤞
If you do face any obstacles building / installing, please submit an issue! 🙏
Note for x86
patolette
ships a slightly modified version of
faiss
to aid with an optional
KMeans
refinement step. You can use the
CMAKE_ARGS
environment variable to specify an instruction set extension for it to be built with. If your CPU supports any of the
AVX
extensions, you can drastically increase
KMeans
performance.
For example, if your CPU supports
AVX512
export
CMAKE_ARGS=
"
-DOPT_LEVEL=avx512
"
The following will build the wheel and install it in the currently active virtual environment.
Linux (Debian)
#
Clone repository
git clone https://github.com/big-nacho/patolette.git
cd
patolette
#
Install dependencies
apt install libopenblas-openmp-dev libflann-dev
#
Optional: set OPT_LEVEL (check Note for x86 section)
#
Accepted values are "generic", "avx2", "avx512", "avx512_spr", "sve"
export
CMAKE_ARGS=
"
-DOPT_LEVEL=avx512
"
#
Build and install wheel
pip install
.
Note on
OpenBLAS
: although any variant should in theory work,
libopenblas-openmp-dev
is recommended. If you have multiple variants installed, you may need to run the following before building for it to be linked properly.
sudo update-alternatives --set libblas.so.3-x86_64-linux-gnu /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/openblas-openmp/libblas.so.3
sudo update-alternatives --set liblapack.so.3-x86_64-linux-gnu /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/openblas-openmp/liblapack.so.3
macOS
#
Clone repository
git clone https://github.com/big-nacho/patolette.git
cd
patolette
#
Install dependencies
brew install libomp flann
#
Make sure system clang is used. If you use brew's clang
#
you may run into libstdc++ issues
export
CC=/usr/bin/clang
export
CXX=/usr/bin/clang++
#
Let CMake find OpenMP
export
OpenMP_ROOT=
$(
brew --prefix
)
/opt/libomp
#
Build and install wheel
pip install
.
Windows
Windows is of course a world of pain (but hey, no judgement if you're into that sort of thing ⛓️).
Small note:
MSVC
doesn't like building
faiss
with
AVX512
. Stick to
AVX2
if you're building with an instruction set extension on, at least until that's fixed. If you don't know what I'm talking about check
Note for x86
.
The following may vary for you here and there, but mostly you should be able to build and install the wheel following these steps:
First, you need
pkg-config
or CMake won't find
flann
.
You can get it
here
or you can install
pkgconfiglite
using
choco
(that's what I did).
Then you need to get
flann
and
OpenBLAS
. You can do this in a variety of ways but an easy one is to use
conda
. You can get (Mini)conda
here
.
With
conda
installed, open
Anaconda Prompt
and type

Install dependencies

Get conda prefix

%CONDA_PREFIX%

44235628.article_summary: **patolette** 是一个 C / Python 颜色量化与抖动库，核心实现了基于加权变体的 Xiaolin Wu 的 PCA 色彩量化器。主要特性包括：避免轴对齐分割、支持 CIEL*u*v* 和 ICtCp 色彩空间、可选的显著图支持以突出视觉重点、可选的 KMeans 优化。该库尚未完善，不建议用于生产环境，但已具备一定可用性。目前没有 PyPI 包，需手动安装。对于 x86 架构，支持通过 CMAKE_ARGS 设置指令集优化（如 AVX512）。提供了在 Linux、macOS 和 Windows 上的安装步骤，但 Windows 下构建较为复杂，建议参考说明。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对示例中几何公理和数论结果之间关系的不同看法

不同观点：
• Tromp认为文章的例子是清晰的，并指出几何公理和数论结果之间的联系是基于两者都属于更广泛的数学公理化方法。他认为这种联系有助于理解数学的统一性，并以“皮亚诺算术”和“塔斯基世界”为例，说明不同数学领域可以通过公理化方法联系起来。

• NoahZuniga则批评这种做法，认为文章将几何公理与数论结果放在一起，容易让人误解为数论结果直接源自几何公理。他指出，这种编排方式可能会导致读者对数学推理过程的误解，特别是对不同数学分支之间逻辑关系的混淆。

补充讨论：
• Tromp进一步通过具体例子（如“皮亚诺算术”和“塔斯基世界”）阐述了数学公理化方法的普遍性，强调不同数学领域可以通过这种方法建立联系，从而展示数学的内在一致性。

• 争议的焦点在于示例的编排是否会导致读者对几何公理和数论结果之间逻辑关系的误解。NoahZuniga担心这种编排会产生误导，而Tromp则认为这种联系是有益且具有教育意义的。

• 讨论还涉及到数学教育中如何有效传达不同数学领域之间的联系和区别，以及如何避免在示例中产生误导性的暗示。

data.title: Dubious Math in Infinite Jest (2009)
data.author: rafaepta
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了《无尽的玩笑》一书中的几个数学错误。作者Mike Strong是一位大卫·福斯特·华莱士的粉丝，他在多次阅读中注意到书中存在少量数学错误，尤其是与概率和组合数学有关的错误。例如，书中错误地计算了一场108局网球比赛以54比54结束的概率，实际概率远高于书中所述。另一个错误是在解释积分中值定理时，书中角色Mike Pemulis错误地将该定理用于核武器分配，而实际上该定理并不提供具体值的计算方法。作者指出这些错误可能只是排版问题或无心之失，并不影响整体阅读体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对《无尽的玩笑》中数学错误是否为故意设置的讨论，以及对作者数学能力的评价。

不同观点：
• 一些读者（如npilk）认为书中的数学错误可能是作者大卫·福斯特·华莱士（DFW）故意设置的，以暗示角色Pemulis并不如他自己想象的那么聪明，且并未完全掌控一切。这种观点得到一种类比的支持，即Pemulis类似于《哈姆雷特》中的Polonious，一个总是犯错的“智者”。
• 另一部分读者（如A_D_E_P_T）则指出，DFW在其他数学相关作品中也曾犯过类似的错误，比如《Everything and More: A Compact History of Infinity》一书中的错误，这可能表明DFW本身的数学能力有限，而非故意设置错误。
• 数学能力较强的读者（如nneonneo）从数学角度详细分析了书中的具体问题，并通过公式和近似值验证了某些错误的实际影响，认为这些错误可能是无意的。
• 有些读者（如arh68）持开放态度，认为错误可能仅仅是打字错误，或者是为了剧情需要，甚至暗示小说中的世界数学规则与现实不同。
• 其他读者（如andy_xor_andrew）则以幽默的方式认为Pemulis这个角色可能就是不擅长数学，从而解释了书中的数学错误。

补充讨论：
• 一些读者（如FL33TW00D）表示，尽管存在数学错误，他们依然享受阅读《无尽的玩笑》，并期待能找到另一本给他们相似感受的书。
• 也有读者（如neuroelectron）表示对《无尽的玩笑》的阅读体验不佳，认为其细节过多且语法笨重，不如其他类似小说（如《万有引力之虹》）值得一读。
• trefoiled提到了书中法语错误的问题，这些错误也被认为是故意的，增加了对书中错误是否有意设置的讨论维度。
• 还有读者（如ProllyInfamous）对DFW的整体写作风格提出批评，认为他的作品虽然可读性强，但期望读者理解过多技术细节，最终让人感觉空虚。

争议焦点：
• 书中的数学错误是否为作者故意设置以反映角色特点，或仅仅是作者数学能力不足的无意错误。
• 读者对DFW作品的整体评价，特别是对技术细节的处理和读者期望的管理。

44237700.article_content:
Dubious Math in Infinite Jest
by
Mike Strong
Let me say, first of all, that I am a huge fan of David Foster Wallace in general and
Infinite Jest
in particular.
On my first reading of
IJ
, I noticed a few mathematical errors but thought little of them.
After reading the essay
Derivative Sport in Torndao Alley
in
A Supposedly Fun Thing I'll Never Do Again
, though, I became curious about why a writer with a clear aptitude for math would include such mistakes in his opus.
Therefore, during my second reading of
IJ
, I made a note of the errors that I noticed.
As it turned out, their number was smaller than I had imagined.
Consequently, I lost interest in this topic until reading DFW's review of a pair of mathematical novels in a scientific journal.
The broad knowledge of math demonstrated by DFW in this article rekindled my curiousity about the errors in
IJ
, and I decided to document them, in case others might be interested.
My list is actually quite short - only four
mistakes, two of which might well be typographical - and I offer no theories about why they appear.
One of the errors is attributable to the omniscient
narrator, while the other three are spoken
by Mike Pemulis.
Both, we can assume, are competent mathematicians.
Before I outline the errors, I must make a logistical note.
Because I am writing this using a simple text editor, I am somewhat symbolically challenged.
Exponentiation will be denoted using a caret (e.g., 2^3 = 8).
Also, I will not even attempt to depict an integral sign or the usual mathematical symbol for combinations, a pair of elongated parenthesis.
I hope this makes the explanations no less understandable.
The first, and perhaps the most interesting error that I noted, appears on page 259 of
IJ
.
The narrator states that the odds of a 108 game tennis match ending in a 54-match-all tie are 1 in 2^27.
This is incorrect by about seven orders of magnitude; in fact, such an outcome is much more likely than the narrator suggests.
The problem of determining the odds is an exercise in probabilty and combinatorics, a fancy mathematical term for systematic counting.
By the laws of probability, the odds of a 108 game match ending in a tie are
(the number of outcomes resulting in a 54-54 tie) / (the total number of possible outcomes).
The denominator in this expression is easy to calculate.
It is simply 2^108 (an example will follow).
The numerator can be found using the concept of combinations.
That is, the correct anwer is the total number of ways team A can be assigned exactly 54 victories out of the 108 matches.
(Of course, if team A wins exactly 54 matches, so must team B.)
In combinatorics this is referred to as "the number of combinations of 108 things taken 54 at a time."
Although the derivation is well beyond the scope of this discussion, it can be shown that the number of combinations of
n
things taken
m
at a time is
n! / ((n-m)! m!)
.
Therefore, the numerator in the probabilty expression above is 108! / (54! * 54!), and the correct odds are
(108! / (54! *54!))/(2^108) or approximately 0.0766.
This is considerably greater than 1/2^27, or about 0.00000000745.
To illustrate this result, consider the following enumerable example:
What are the odds of a 4 game match ending in a 2-2 tie?
Again, the method above predicts that odds are
(4! / (2! * 2!))/(2^4)
=
(24 / (2 * 2))/(16)
= 6/16.
The answer suggested by the narrator of
IJ
would be 1/(2^1) = 1/2.
To see which is correct, we can list all 16 possible outcomes as follows:
AAAA
ABAA
BAAA
BBAA
AAAB
ABAB
BAAB
BBAB
AABA
ABBA
BABA
BBBA
AABB
ABBB
BABB
BBBB
Clearly, there are six outcomes resulting in a 2-2 tie (AABB, ABAB, ABBA, BAAB, BABA, and BBAA), so the odds are, indeed, 6/16 as the method above predicts.
The second significant instance of dubious math in
IJ
occurs in a footnote on pages 1023 and 1024.
In this section Mike Pemulis describes to Hal how the Mean Value Theorem for integrals can be used to distribute megatons of thermonuclear weapons among Eschaton combatants.
The Mean Value Theorem for integrals states that, for a function
f(x)
that is continunous on the interval from
x = a
to
x = b
,
the integral from
a
to
b
of
f(x)dx = f(x')(b - a)
for some value
x'
between
a
and
b.
In effect, this theorem simply states that the area underneath the curve described by the function
f(x)
from
x = a
to
x = b
is exactly the same as the area of a rectangle whose width extends from
a
to
b
and whose height has a value of
f(x')
for some value
x'
between
a
and
b
.
Now, while Pemulis' description of the theorem is essential correct, the problem in this footnote is the way the theorem is supposedly applied.
Specifically, the Mean Value Theorem for integrals is a theoretical tool for proving the
existence
of this particular
x'.
It does not, however, offer any method of finding the
value
of
x'
.
Therefore, it is difficult to imagine how the Mean Value Theorem for integrals could be employed in Pemulis' Eschaton calculations.
Incidently, the third, minor

• 另一部分读者（如A_D_E_P_T）则指出，DFW在其他数学相关作品中也曾犯过类似的错误，比如《Everything and More: A Compact History of Infinity》一书中的错误，这可能表明DFW本身的数学能力有限，而非故意设置错误。
• 数学能力较强的读者（如nneonneo）从数学角度详细分析了书中的具体问题，并通过公式和近似值验证了某些错误的实际影响，认为这些错误可能是无意的。
• 有些读者（如arh68）持开放态度，认为错误可能仅仅是打字错误，或者是为了剧情需要，甚至暗示小说中的世界数学规则与现实不同。
• 其他读者（如andy_xor_andrew）则以幽默的方式认为Pemulis这个角色可能就是不擅长数学，从而解释了书中的数学错误。

补充讨论：
• 一些读者（如FL33TW00D）表示，尽管存在数学错误，他们依然享受阅读《无尽的玩笑》，并期待能找到另一本给他们相似感受的书。
• 也有读者（如neuroelectron）表示对《无尽的玩笑》的阅读体验不佳，认为其细节过多且语法笨重，不如其他类似小说（如《万有引力之虹》）值得一读。
• trefoiled提到了书中法语错误的问题，这些错误也被认为是故意的，增加了对书中错误是否有意设置的讨论维度。
• 还有读者（如ProllyInfamous）对DFW的整体写作风格提出批评，认为他的作品虽然可读性强，但期望读者理解过多技术细节，最终让人感觉空虚。

争议焦点：
• 书中的数学错误是否为作者故意设置以反映角色特点，或仅仅是作者数学能力不足的无意错误。
• 读者对DFW作品的整体评价，特别是对技术细节的处理和读者期望的管理。

不同观点：
• **支持与赞赏**：
  - 有人赞赏Raph Levien及其团队在Vellum项目上的长期努力和创新精神，认为他们在推动2D渲染方面做出了有价值的尝试，尤其是对UI渲染的深入研究（如[littlestymaar]）。
  - 有人对Vellum的性能和设计表示赞赏，认为其从一开始就注重渲染效率是值得肯定的（如[boxerab]和[jasonthorsness]）。

• **技术质疑与改进建议**：
  - [coffeeaddict1]指出Vellum在当前API和GPU合作水平上的局限性，并提到Pathfinder和Blend2D等已有技术，质疑Vellum是否真的有显著进步。
  - [morio]详细分析了Vellum的实现细节，指出了潜在的计算问题和渲染伪影，建议采用更先进的色彩空间和处理方式。

• **技术比较**：
  - [krona]将Vellum与SLUG算法及WDOPB的矢量纹理方法进行比较，质疑其实时计算的可行性和相对于已有方案的优势。
  - [pier25]将Vellum与Rive进行比较，询问其性能上的差异。

  - [taneq]对瓦片生成和排序的效率提出疑问，认为可能有更早期的优化方法。
  - [leetrout]对GPU术语和路径填充的判断方法表示困惑，希望了解更多技术细节。

  - [xixixao]和[haniehz]则关注其他方面，如个人项目解释和简单赞赏。
  - [s-mon]询问这些方法是否可以应用于3D。
  - [Fraterkes]提到Rust与荷兰的关联，并询问Raph的新样条曲线在工具中的应用情况。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点主要集中在Vellum项目的实际性能提升和相对于其他已有技术的优势。
- 对Vellum实现细节的讨论，尤其是色彩空间、渲染伪影和算法效率等问题。
- 对GPU渲染技术的基本概念和细节的深入探讨，如路径填充和瓦片排序的效率问题。

data.title: Denuvo Analysis
data.author: StefanBatory
data.article_summary:
这篇文章详细分析了Denuvo，一种成功的反篡改和数字版权管理（DRM）系统，主要用于保护游戏不被盗版和逆向工程。Denuvo通过独特的硬件验证和加密技术，确保游戏代码的完整性。其工作流程包括：

1. 首次启动程序时，Denuvo收集硬件信息并发送至服务器。
2. 服务器处理后返回一个许可证文件，包含加密常量和硬件信息。
3. 程序之后使用该文件进行本地验证，无需再次联网。
4. 程序执行时会检查当前硬件信息是否匹配，若不匹配则导致游戏崩溃。

Denuvo通过将部分指令移除并加密，存储在许可证文件中，只有合法用户才能正确解密并执行原始游戏指令。该系统复杂且难以破解，但也引发了对用户体验的争议。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Denuvo DRM的技术细节、有效性及其影响

不同观点：
• **Denuvo的技术遗产与问题**：farmdve认为Denuvo继承了SecuROM时代的遗留技术（如UD2），并指出这种技术可能导致某些游戏在未来无法运行。他还详细解释了CPUID钩子与Windows异常处理的冲突问题，说明Denuvo在未来可能导致兼容性问题。
• **Denuvo的复杂性与混淆技术**：yukIttEft通过使用LLVM分解Denuvo的x86混淆代码，揭示其如何将游戏代码转换为基于栈机的虚拟机代码，并指出其中的多重赋值和混淆操作（如MBAs），使得破解非常困难。他还询问是否有LLVM优化器可以处理MBAs。
• **Denuvo的有效性**：rjh29认为Denuvo非常有效，因为即便在多年后，受Denuvo保护的游戏仍然未被破解，显示其强大的防破解能力。
• **独立开发者的DRM技术与市场困境**：2c2c2c分享了一个独立开发者朋友开发类似Denuvo的DRM技术但难以商业化的故事，并寻求建议。
• **消费者抵制与用户体验**：shmerl和tristor等用户主张通过不购买带有Denuvo的游戏来抵制这种DRM，tristor进一步表示Denuvo使得在Linux系统上玩游戏变得不可能，因此他拒绝购买相关游戏。mdaniel则抱怨Denuvo对正版用户的体验造成了负面影响。
• **对"盗版常量"或"盗版指令"的困惑**：flerchin对使用"stolen constants"或"stolen instructions"这样的术语表示困惑，认为用"拦截"可能更合适。
• **对Empress和破解社区的讨论**：Traubenfuchs提到了著名的Denuvo破解者Empress，并对其在网络上的古怪表现进行了评论，而larodi和cainxinth则期待Empress的分析。
• **DRM与游戏产业的未来**：doctorpangloss认为Denuvo为单人PC游戏提供了防盗版选项，并指出游戏产业可以选择多人在线或其他环境完整性技术来防止盗版。他还认为反对Denuvo的运动具有讽刺意味，因为Denuvo实际上保护了那些希望通过单人游戏获取收益的开发者。

补充讨论：
• **对DRM和游戏价值的广泛看法**：menthe认为DRM只是繁琐的技术工作，不值得重视，并认为大多数AAA游戏不值得玩，推荐独立游戏或经典游戏。
• **对技术复杂性和创新的讨论**：一些评论提到了Denuvo复杂的混淆技术（如MBAs）以及破解过程中的技术挑战，反映了DRM开发与破解之间的技术对抗。

争议焦点：
• **Denuvo对正版用户体验的影响**：一部分用户（如mdaniel和tristor）认为Denuvo严重影响了正版用户的体验，而另一部分用户（如doctorpangloss）则认为Denuvo对游戏产业的防盗版措施至关重要，并认为反对Denuvo的运动忽视了开发者的利益。

44226406.article_content:
Denuvo Analysis
Posted on
2025-01-21
• 3805 words
• 18 minute read
Foreword
This post is intended for educational purposes only. Denuvo is arguably the most successful digital rights management solution to have ever existed, and is therefore an interest to many. This blog contains a large amount of my personal notes and correspondence with other reverse engineers (see
kudos
) which contains information about the recent iterations of Denuvo, lots of which I haven’t seen shared publicly before.
I mean no harm towards Irdeto and thus certain information will be redacted from this post.
Denuvo
Denuvo is an anti-tamper and digital rights management system (DRM). It is primarily used to protect digital media such as video games from piracy and reverse engineering efforts. Unlike traditional DRM systems, Denuvo employs a wide range of unique techniques and checks to confirm the integrity of both the game’s code and licensed user.
The General Idea
The core idea behind Denuvo is nothing new. It can only be described as a semi-online DRM for reasons that will become clear shortly. The general idea is as follows:
(1)
User boots program.exe for the first time.
(2)
Before any original game code is executed, Denuvo will collect hardware identification information regarding the current system, and prepare it for sending over the internet.
(3)
program.exe then sends this hardware information to a Denuvo hosted server. What occurs at the server is obviously a mystery, but it likely applies reversible mathematical functions to combine the “stolen constants” (more on those later) with the hardware information provided by program.exe. The server then sends this now mixed information, we will refer to this as “the license file”, back to program.exe.
(4)
Once program.exe receives the license file, a local copy is created that program.exe can refer to on future boots; removing the need for another online request to be made (hence the use of “semi-online” earlier).
(5)
program.exe will be redirected to the original entry point (OEP) and begin executing the actual game code. During this time, program.exe will collect hardware information at runtime and attempt to decrypt stolen constants from the license file. These now decrypted constants will then be used to execute “original game instructions”.
If it wasn’t made clear already, the game will effectively end up performing user integrity checks. This is due to the fact that if the hardware information collected at runtime is not the equal to that of which was used to create the license file on the Denuvo server, then an incorrect stolen constant will be decrypted and the game will likely suffer (most of the time this is a direct crash).
A More Technical Explanation
This section will investigate each protection mechanism and user integrity check more thoroughly. Remember, there is far more to Denuvo that what is outlined here.
General Idea Revisited
License File
When Denuvo is first added to a binary, certain functions in that game are selected to become “protected”. All this means is that the function itself will be executed inside of a virtual machine, and select parts of certain instructions will be removed entirely from the binary. The license file is simply all of these removed bytes combined together and combined with the user’s hardware identification via reversible mathematical functions. It is important that whatever operations are applied are reversible, otherwise the client would have no way of decrypting and getting the original constant.
License DWORDs
Since there are multiple stolen instructions, prior to handling execution over to the OEP, Denuvo will write select parts of the license file into DWORDs, scattered around the .vm section (.vm being the PE section which contains the VM code). Each DWORD, we will nick “License DWORD”, is effectively a single instruction that was removed from the binary, combined with the hardware identification information of the customer.

3. 程序之后使用该文件进行本地验证，无需再次联网。
4. 程序执行时会检查当前硬件信息是否匹配，若不匹配则导致游戏崩溃。

Denuvo通过将部分指令移除并加密，存储在许可证文件中，只有合法用户才能正确解密并执行原始游戏指令。该系统复杂且难以破解，但也引发了对用户体验的争议。

data.title: A Primer on Molecular Dynamics
data.author: EvgeniyZh
data.article_summary: 这篇文章是关于分子动力学（MD）的入门介绍。MD通过模拟分子在原子层面的动态行为，帮助研究人员观察分子的运动，而不仅仅是通过实验获得静态图像。MD可用于预测分子行为，例如药物与靶点的结合强度或酶的设计。然而，学习MD非常困难，因为它涉及复杂的物理知识。文章介绍了MD的基本原理，包括系统定义、力场、能量最小化、平衡化以及生产模拟等步骤。此外，文章还讨论了如何绕过小时间尺度问题、量子效应和自由能计算。最后，通过两个案例研究展示了MD在实际研究中的应用，如发现选择性抑制剂和表征受体灵活性。文章旨在帮助读者理解MD的基础理论并能够运行简单的模拟。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：分子动力学（MD）在生物学和药物发现中的重要性及其技术挑战

不同观点：
• 第一种观点：强调分子运动在生物学中至关重要，所有生物系统本质上都是原子的振动和分子运动。理解这一点对于跨领域（如编程进入生物学领域）的人尤为关键。分子生物学中的过程如DNA转录和蛋白质功能都受到物理环境和分子动态的显著影响，这超越了单纯的信息学分析。

• 第二种观点：在药物发现中的计算机辅助设计（CAD）工具开发中，MD是一个极具挑战性且有趣的领域。然而，验证MD行为的实验数据非常复杂，尤其是通过核磁共振（NMR）数据推断蛋白质的动态。实验验证MD模型非常困难，因为大多数数据是静态的晶体结构，缺乏动态信息。

• 第三种观点：提供了由DE Shaw制作的关于分子动力学模拟的视频资源，认为该视频内容易于理解且非常有趣，适合对MD感兴趣的人作为学习材料。

• 第四种观点：指出用于MD模拟的软件通常是由科学家编写的不优化代码，杂乱且难以维护。目前没有单一的技术高手能够彻底解决这一问题。

• 第五种观点：认为MD是科学计算的良好入门领域，简单的模拟容易实现，但性能扩展存在挑战。推荐了几个流行的MD引擎和分析工具，如Amber、Gromacs和MDAnalysis，并提供了相关文档和资源链接。

补充讨论：
• 提到MD领域中“粗粒化”方法的重要性，并表示希望有更多相关资料。同时，反映初学者在学习如Amber手册时的困难，尽管其内容丰富，但组织结构不够便利。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在MD模型的实验验证困难和软件工具的优化问题上。实验数据的复杂性和软件代码的杂乱性是当前MD研究和应用中的主要挑战。

Introduction
I’ve recently become very interested in molecular dynamics, or MD.
Why would you want to do MD at all? MD allow you to watch molecules dance in full atomic detail. While experimental techniques give you static molecular mugshots, MD lets you observe the dynamic behavior of molecules over time. And understanding molecular motion is key for everything in biology,
everything
in biology is vibrating molecules underneath the surface! Beyond just watching, you can use MD to predict molecular behavior. Want to know how tightly a drug will bind its target? Run an MD simulation and calculate the binding free energy. Trying to design a new enzyme? Simulate different designs to see which folds and functions best. Obviously, there are limitations — as we’ll get into — but the possibilities the field presents are fascinating.
Unfortunately, MD also happens to be incredibly hard to learn on your own. Unlike my other posts, where I can go from nearly zero knowledge to blog-post-capable in a week, MD has taken me the better part of a month and I’m
still
unsure of a lot of things. I’m much more used to the general fuzziness of ML; extremely overparameterized statistical models that can actively learn means that their exact theoretical underpinnings are, at best, interesting, but rarely useful outside of a few cases. So, hand-waving is practically fine! This isn’t the case in MD, all of it feels important to know and understand. You’re dealing with physics after all, and even if you hand-wave away certain aspects of the physics, your simplified model will be that much less capable of understanding certain phenomena.
In this post, I’ll try to equip you with enough knowledge to run basic simulations on your own, while also having enough theoretical backing to understand what’s actually going on under the surface. Obviously, we’ll be skipping a lot of things, but there should be enough here to vaguely understand some MD papers! To test this out, we’ll also go over two MD papers at the end of the post.
How does MD work in practice?
Consider a protein that we dreamed up. Completely unfolded, just a straight line of amino-acids linked together, Glycine-Lysine-Alanine, and so on. What happens if we drop this protein in a bucket of water and wait a few hundred nanoseconds? It’ll slowly turn from a straight line into a knotted mess of tangles and curves. Or, in other words, it will
fold.
Most people will be familiar with the concept of a protein folding, the Alphafold2 news-cycle hammered that into most of us. But it's worth considering what it means for a protein to 'want' to fold at all. In many ways, a protein 'wants' to fold in the same way a dropped apple 'wants' to fall to the ground — physics simply pulls it in that direction. In the case of the apple, gravity is making the biggest call. In the case of the protein, the forces at play are more at the molecular level. Here are some:
Bond forces
: Chemical attachments between neighboring atoms that can be stretched, twisted, or turned to different angles.
Electrostatic interactions
: Attractions or repulsion between charged atoms.
Van der Waals forces
: Weak electromagnetic attractions between all atoms in close proximity
Solvent interactions
: Some parts of a protein may be hydrophobic/hydrophilic and will desire to hide its hydrophobic elements away from water + expose its hydrophilic elements to water.
There’s a few more of course, but these are the major ones. These forces will push and pull on every atom contained in the protein, ultimately forcing it to a certain configuration. As mentioned, this final configuration is the folded state of the protein, but we could interpret this final state in a more physics-grounded way:
low thermodynamic free energy.
It’s not worth pondering too much
how
to quantitatively assess this, but rest assured there are, we’ll discuss it a bit more later. Low thermodynamic free energy of a folded structure means it’s a stable structure (hard to move from), and high means its an unstable structure (easy to move from).
To note, the above pushing-pulling on our protein isn’t just the case for protein folding, it’s for all problems! D

data.title: Finding Atari Games in Randomly Generated Data
data.author: wanderingjew
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了通过随机数据生成并筛选出可能的Atari 2600游戏的实验项目。作者利用GPU生成数十亿个4KB的随机数据文件，通过模拟器运行并筛选出潜在的游戏。由于Atari 2600游戏卡带数据量有限，理论上有极大量的可能组合，但绝大多数是无意义的。为提高效率，作者使用了一些启发式方法，如检查有效操作码（opcode）的频率，以过滤掉明显的无用数据。最终，通过这种大规模随机生成和筛选，找到了一些有趣但未必有实际价值的"游戏"。该项目展示了利用现代计算能力探索巨大可能性空间的过程。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：随机生成有效ROM并探索其可能性

不同观点：
• **selcuka**：分享了一个个人经历，讲述了由于磁带加载错误，意外修改了游戏代码，导致游戏无限续命。他认为这种情况虽然不如从头写一个游戏的概率低，但仍然很有趣。
• **jerf**：认为通过在生成阶段使用接受标准来优化随机ROM生成是一种有效的方法，相当于快速生成有意义的输出，而不是浪费资源在无用的结果上。
• **staplung**：将该实验比作博尔赫斯的《巴别图书馆》，并通过计算指出可能的ROM组合数量巨大，甚至超过可观测宇宙的规模。
• **a_cardboard_box**：指出这些随机生成的ROM虽然在模拟器上显示动态或结构化数据，但不太可能在实际的电视或游戏机上正确运行，尤其是由于VSync信号问题。
• **tdjsnelling**：赞赏这个概念，并提到自己的项目“Library of Babel”应用。
• **JetSetIlly**：提到最简单的2600游戏只有2K大小，如Combat，建议限制大小为2K以增加找到完整ROM的机会。
• **edent**：幽默地提到在实验中可能会忽视外界的重要变化，如星星熄灭。
• **mjd**：认为这是他见过的“最愚蠢”但令人惊叹的项目之一。
• **xhrpost**：提到类似的项目“Pulling JPEGs From Thin Air”，通过随机生成数据来产生有效图像。
• **jsnider3**：建议通过从Atari游戏的汇编代码中随机采样来生成游戏，而不是依赖LLM生成。
• **coldcity**：分享了自己以前做过类似的实验，使用32字节的DOS程序和基本的遗传编程。
• **p0w3n3d**：质疑从随机生成游戏到生成可在Atari上运行的内容的转变，认为随机生成的数据可能包含部分游戏元素，但不太可能生成完整游戏。
• **mock-possum**：对实验结果感到兴奋，希望作者能进一步探索可能出现的结果。
• **_benj**：认为这是一个非常有趣的实验，提到自己曾做过类似的实验，探索理性数模式。
• **wannabebarista**：认为项目有趣，但对模拟器产生的噪音感到惊吓。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是随机生成数据是否能真正生成有效的、可运行的游戏ROM。
• 讨论中多次提到博尔赫斯的《巴别图书馆》，将其作为理解随机生成巨大可能性的比喻。
• 对项目实际运行效果和在不同设备上的表现存在一定质疑，尤其是实际电视和游戏机上的运行情况。
• 对优化随机生成过程的方法进行了探讨，包括使用接受标准和限制ROM大小。
• 项目被普遍认为有趣且具有探索价值，但也有人对其实际效果持怀疑态度。

Finding Atari Games in Randomly Generated Data
TL;DR,
here’s the GitHub repo
This project generated around 30 Billion individual 4kB files of random data. These files were winnowed down to about 10,000 through some heuristics gleaned from the complete collection of Atari ROM files. Finally, a classifier system scanned them using an Atari 2600 emulator to see if any of these random files were actually an Atari game. This project answers a question no one asked, no one wanted, and is a massive waste of resources: What if I shove a billion monkeys in a GPU and asked them to write a game for the Atari 2600?
Thanks to advances in GPUs, AI, and machine learning, we can now (very quickly) write a Python script that dumps garbage into 4KB ROMs and asks,
“does this look like a game?”
This isn’t nostalgia, because my first console was an NES. This is about exploring something unimaginably vast and seeing if anything weird falls out.
Results First
Because no one reads below the fold, here’s an interactive emulator showcasing the most interesting Atari ROMs discovered. There’s no genetic algorithm here; just billions of random files run through an emulator. These are the best of the weird:
WARNING: turn your volume down. There’s a bug in
EmulatorJS
.
Problem Scope
Assume each Atari 2600 cartridge is a 4 kilobyte chunk of data. It’s a maximum of 4096 bytes, or 32,768 bits. That means there are $2^{32768}$ possible ROMs. For perspective:
That’s $10^{10159}$ potential Atari games.
There are about $10^{20}$ grains of sand on Earth.
And roughly $10^{80}$ protons in the visible universe.
If you turned an entire datacenter of AI compute boxes onto this problem, it would likely take years before anything interesting was found. But with a little bit of smarts and actually reading a datasheet, the problem set is massively reduced. The basic search path to finding a ‘random’ Atari game would be to:
Generate a ROM, by dumping 4kB of data from /dev/random into a file.
Run that file in an emulator
Capture a screenshot or five
Filter or score them with AI
Save the best results for further investigation.
This would work, if we had enough time to wait for black holes to devour the Universe. A better idea would be to front-load the pipeline with some simple checks to discard the absolute garbage before spinning up an emulator. It would help to know what a real Atari ROM would look like, simply to build some heuristics.
Heuristics
I’m not going to emulate every possible ROM. I’m trying to find the
interesting
ones. This means filtering, and being smart about what we’re doing:
Opcode Sanity
The 6507 CPU (from here on out I’m calling it a 6502, to make you, specifically, angry) has 151 valid opcodes, and these opcodes are going to be all over the first half of the ROM. First I should check if there are a lot of opcodes in the data. These opcodes are:
0x00, 0x01, 0x05, 0x06, 0x08, 0x09, 0x0A, 0x0D, 0x0E, 0x10, 0x11, 0x15, 0x16, 0x18,

44236900.article_summary: 本文介绍了通过随机数据生成并筛选出可能的Atari 2600游戏的实验项目。作者利用GPU生成数十亿个4KB的随机数据文件，通过模拟器运行并筛选出潜在的游戏。由于Atari 2600游戏卡带数据量有限，理论上有极大量的可能组合，但绝大多数是无意义的。为提高效率，作者使用了一些启发式方法，如检查有效操作码（opcode）的频率，以过滤掉明显的无用数据。最终，通过这种大规模随机生成和筛选，找到了一些有趣但未必有实际价值的"游戏"。该项目展示了利用现代计算能力探索巨大可能性空间的过程。

data.title: New Quantum Algorithm Factors Numbers with One Qubit
data.author: isaacfrond
data.article_summary: 一篇新论文提出了一种使用单个量子比特（qubit）和三个振荡器来分解整数的新量子算法。尽管传统上分解大数需要大量量子比特和复杂的量子计算机，这项新方法通过利用连续变量编码信息，实现了仅用一个量子比特分解任意大小的整数。然而，该方法并不实用，因为它需要相当于几颗中等大小恒星的能量。这一研究挑战了传统计算思维，展示了量子计算解决问题的全新途径，尽管目前不具备实际应用价值。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：

New Quantum Algorithm Factors Numbers With One Qubit
By
Stephen Ornes
June 9, 2025
The catch: It would require the energy of a few medium-size stars.

A new quantum algorithm flies in the face of intuition.
Celsius Pictor for
Quanta Magazine

By
Stephen Ornes
Contributing Writer

View PDF/Print Mode
algorithms

All topics
Quantum computers still can’t do much. Almost every time researchers have found something the high-tech machines should one day excel at, a
classical algorithm comes along
that can do it just as well on a regular computer. One notable exception? Taking apart numbers. In 1994, the mathematician Peter Shor devised an algorithm that would let
quantum computers factor big numbers exponentially faster
than classical machines. That speedup matters because a fast-factoring algorithm could render most data-encryption methods useless. For more than 30 years, researchers have been trying to boost and
guard against the power of future quantum computers
.
But Shor’s factoring algorithm also has limitations: The bigger the number you want to factor, the bigger and better the quantum computer you need. Cracking an encryption scheme would require a quantum computer running Shor’s algorithm on
hundreds of thousands
of efficient quantum bits, or qubits. Today’s machines are nowhere close.
But a
paper
posted to the scientific preprint site arxiv.org describes how to factor any number with considerably fewer qubits: just one. In the new work, researchers show how to factor an integer of any size with a single qubit and three components known as oscillators — readily available devices typically associated with other quantum technology, like optics systems.
To be clear, it’s not a practical advance: The process requires exponentially more energy than a million-qubit quantum computer. But it does illuminate new ways of solving these kinds of problems. “This departs from the typical way we think about computing — and not just quantum computing, but classical computing as well,” said
Ulysse Chabaud
, a computer scientist at the École Normale Supérieure in Paris who did not work on the new approach. “This seems crazy, if not impossible.”
Good Oscillations
Ultimately, the new approach works because of how it encodes information. Classical computers use bits, which can take one of two values. Qubits, the quantum equivalent, can take on multiple values, because of the vagaries of quantum mechanics. But even qubits, once measured, can take on only one of two values, a 0 or a 1.
But that’s not the only way to encode data in quantum devices, say
Robert König
and
Lukas Brenner
of the Technical University of Munich. Their work focuses on ways to encode information with continuous variables, meaning they can take on any values in a given range, instead of just certain ones.

From left: Lukas Brenner, Libor Caha and Robert König, along with Xavier Coiteux-Roy (not pictured), devised a novel but impractical way to factor any integer with a single qubit.
C. Hohmann/Munich Center for Quantum Science and Technology
In the past, researchers have tried to improve on Shor’s algorithm for factoring by simulating a qubit using a continuous system, with its expanded set of possible values. But even if your system computes with continuous qubits, it will still need a lot of them to factor numbers, and it won’t necessarily go any faster. “We were wondering whether there’s a better way of using continuous variable systems,” König said.
They decided to go back to basics. The secret to Shor’s algorithm is that it uses the number it’s factoring to generate what researchers call a periodic function, which has repeating values at regular intervals. Then it uses a mathematical tool called a quantum Fourier transform to identify the value of that period — how long it takes for the function to repeat. From there, some straightforward algebra can reveal the original number’s factors.

Those patterns act like a built-in quantum Fourier transform, said König.

data.title: The Concurrency Trap: How an Atomic Counter Stalled a Pipeline
data.author: delifue
data.article_summary: Conviva的流媒体分析平台在2月2日遭遇了一个客户的P99延迟激增问题。平台每天处理5万亿事件，由基于DAG（有向无环图）的分析引擎驱动，每个客户的逻辑都被编译成DAG，在Tokio上的自定义actor模型中并发运行。最初的调试未找到明显原因，进一步分析通过保存事件数据并在perf环境中重现问题，最终发现瓶颈在于一个共享类型注册表中的原子计数器。该计数器在并发哈希表（flashmap）中用于读取保护，导致大量上下文切换和处理时间增加。尽管flashmap理论上更适合读多写少的场景，但替换为dashmap并未解决问题。最终，分析火焰图发现问题在于高频的原子操作（AtomicUsize::fetch_sub），导致并发处理时性能下降。此次调查揭示了并发、缓存线及适当数据结构的重要性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：并发数据结构的实现与性能优化，特别是ArcSwap和RCU（Read-Copy-Update）机制的应用。

不同观点：
• nasretdinov认为Go语言的并发哈希表（sync.Map）已经实现了类似功能，无需每次复制整个哈希表，并且实现得很优雅。
• hinkley指出ArcSwap与并发哈希表的不同之处在于ArcSwap在写入时需要替换整个底层数据，但读取非常便宜。他还提到树数据结构的优势，并提出混合ArcSwap和DashMap的设想，利用分片写时复制来解决写竞争问题。
• nick_关注缓存伪共享问题，指出通过将计数器变量单独放在一个缓存行上可以减少不必要的缓存乒乓效应。
• hinkley进一步分析了在高并发环境下的排队理论效应，指出一旦队列建立起来，清理时间会比直觉预期长得多。
• kccqzy对用户空间实现RCU的有效性提出质疑，认为缺少内核支持可能导致难以安全地释放数据结构。
• athrowaway3z表示ArcSwap的代码比预期的要复杂，不符合其心理模型。
• cryptonector详细解释了TFA中的并发哈希表问题及其解决方案，包括使用RCU和写时复制数据结构，并分享了自己实现类似数据结构的经验，强调了原子操作和垃圾收集的复杂性。
• vrosas对问题追踪时间过长表示惊讶，认为缺乏遥测和领域知识是主要问题。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及多种技术方案，包括ArcSwap、DashMap、RCU、Hazard Pointers等，体现了对不同并发数据结构实现方法的深入探讨。
• 争议的焦点之一是如何有效解决写竞争和缓存乒乓效应，以及在用户空间实现RCU的可行性。
• 实际应用中的性能问题和调试难度也被提及，反映出在复杂系统中定位和解决问题的挑战。

44208938.article_content:
On February 2nd, Conviva’s streaming analytics platform suddenly ground to a crawl but only for one customer. P99 latency spiked without clear reason, pushing our DAG engine to its limits. What started as a puzzling slowdown soon became a deep dive into concurrency pitfalls.
Conviva’s platform is built to handle
5 trillion daily events
, powered by a
DAG
(directed acyclic graph) based analytics engine. Each customer’s logic is compiled into a DAG, running concurrently on a custom actor model built atop Tokio.
This post unpacks how a seemingly innocuous atomic counter in a shared type registry became the bottleneck and what we learned about concurrency, cache lines, and the right data structures for the job. If you use Rust at scale, or plan to, you’ll enjoy this.
Setting The Stage
We initially tried debugging the issue by eliminating the obvious causes – watermarking, inaccurate metrics etc.
Traffic from gateway showing the P99 latency spike
There was some spirited discussion around whether the way the Tokio runtime was scheduling its tasks across physical threads was causing issues but that seemed improbable given that we use an actor system and each DAG processing task runs independently on a specific actor, and it was unlikely that multiple actors were being scheduled onto the same underlying physical thread.
There were additional lines of inquiry around whether HDFS writes were what was causing the lag to build up and eventually causing a backpressure throughout the system. More analysis of more graphs showed increased context switching during the incident but still with no clear evidence of the cause.
Analyzing The Evidence
We were able to reproduce the issue by saving the event data to GCS buckets and replaying this in an environment enabled with perf. This was a relief because at least the issue wasn’t tied to the prod environment, which would have been a nightmare to debug.
We track active sessions across our system, so we have a reasonable measure of how much load our system is under. However, further analysis in the perf environment revealed that while there was a spike in the number of active sessions, those gradually dropped off while the DAG processing time continued to stay high.
Session count tracker and processing time
While this was still puzzling, at least we had a clear indication of where to look – inside our DAG compiler/engine. All the clues pointed to this as being the source of the issue for the P99 latency spike and the backpressure we were seeing throughout the system.
While we knew where to look, this investigation had already taken weeks and things took a turn for the worse when we hit the issue again on February 23rd. However, there was more evidence coming our way about where to look. All Grafana metrics pointed to DAG processing actually being the cause of slowdown. Another interesting graph that came up was this one displaying the jump in context switches during the incident. While it didn’t lead us directly to the root cause at that point, it became important later on as we identified the issue and resolved it because it tied in neatly with our analysis.
Context switches
Recreating The Crime Scene
Thanks to the earlier work in recreating the issue in a perf environment, we were able to generate these flamegraphs that highlighted hot paths in the code. The first one displays the flamegraph during normal traffic and the second one displays the flamegraph during the incident.
Normal traffic flamegraph
Incident traffic flamegraph
In the incident flamegraph, you can clearly see the dreaded wide bars which indicate longer processing time.
Looking carefully at the flamegraph generated during the incident, you can see a very high load for call paths involving
AtomicUsize::fetch_sub
which was being called from creating and dropping a
ReadGuard
in
flashmap
, which we were using as a concurrent hash map. This concurrent hash map was being used as a type registry which was globally shared amongst all DAG’s across our system.
In the context of this, the earlier graph about the context switches spiking during the incident makes some sense. The
ReadGuard
in the hot path of the flamegraph was responsible for handling reads from various threads and each thread would increment and decrement the counter.
Now, one important thing about the hashmap in the type registry is that it is
almost
read-only. It is initialized with some types on start-up and then only updated when a new type is seen but that rarely ever happened. However, on a critical path, it would check to see if the type was already registered which is where the atomic increments and decrements were occurring.
Now, the question was what to do about this. In the
flashmap documentation

dashmap
performed better in terms of both latency & throughput. Unfortunately, replacing
flashmap
with

44208938.article_summary: Conviva的流媒体分析平台在2月2日遭遇了一个客户的P99延迟激增问题。平台每天处理5万亿事件，由基于DAG（有向无环图）的分析引擎驱动，每个客户的逻辑都被编译成DAG，在Tokio上的自定义actor模型中并发运行。最初的调试未找到明显原因，进一步分析通过保存事件数据并在perf环境中重现问题，最终发现瓶颈在于一个共享类型注册表中的原子计数器。该计数器在并发哈希表（flashmap）中用于读取保护，导致大量上下文切换和处理时间增加。尽管flashmap理论上更适合读多写少的场景，但替换为dashmap并未解决问题。最终，分析火焰图发现问题在于高频的原子操作（AtomicUsize::fetch_sub），导致并发处理时性能下降。此次调查揭示了并发、缓存线及适当数据结构的重要性。

• nick_关注缓存伪共享问题，指出通过将计数器变量单独放在一个缓存行上可以减少不必要的缓存乒乓效应。

data.author: enescakir
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要介绍了在斯坦福大学的国家安全政策课程《Technology, Innovation and Great Power Competition》中如何整合和应用人工智能（AI）技术。课程旨在让学生为未来AI广泛应用的职业环境做好准备。文章概述了AI在课程中的具体使用方式、学生的应用实例以及师生从中的学习收获。通过这种创新教学方法，学生能更好地理解和应对大国科技竞争中的国家安全政策问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在政策学习中的应用及其效果

不同观点：
• **支持观点：**
   - **suddenlybananas**: 认为AI可以帮助政策学生处理大量文档，包括总结内容、识别主题、进行深度分析，并应用于解决具体政策问题。
   - **示例**: 假设学生团队可以使用AI来提升学习效率。

• **质疑观点：**
   - **radioactivist**: 质疑AI的实际能力，指出在演示中AI无法完成所声称的任务，反而要求用户自行查找信息。
   - **示例**: AI在演示中多次表示无法完成任务，要求查看相关网站。

• **评价标准缺失：**
   - **cptroot**: 指出文章缺乏对AI加速学习效果的评估标准，无法判断AI对学习过程的实际帮助。
   - **troelsSteegin**: 认为缺少对比数据，无法了解使用AI工具前后的学习体验差异。

• **学习效果质疑：**
   - **bjelkeman-again**: 担心AI工具被用作不阅读文档的捷径，质疑学生是否能从中真正学到并保留知识。
   - **示例**: 使用AI工具是否会导致学生只是得到结果而未真正理解内容。

• **幽默批评：**
   - **psunavy03**: 以幽默方式批评那些将“阅读”任务交给AI的人。
   - **示例**: 引用军校笑话，暗示只有真正去做才算完成阅读。

• **反对依赖AI：**
   - **bgwalter**: 反对依赖AI，认为直接阅读原始信息并自己整理更有效，特别是在涉及军事和经济等重要领域时。
   - **示例**: 推荐阅读Mearsheimer和智库政策文件，认为这些比AI工具更可靠。

• **对工具准确性的怀疑：**
   - **OWaz**: 对人们轻易依赖AI工具并相信其准确性感到困惑。
   - **示例**: 质疑人们为何如此信任AI的准确性。

• **对AI和国家安全领域的批评：**
   - **einpoklum**: 批评国家安全和AI领域充满炒作和自封的专家，质疑其用于公众操纵的目的。
   - **示例**: 指出这两个领域被用于可疑的公众操纵目的。

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点**: AI在政策学习中的实际效果和应用价值受到广泛质疑，尤其是其实际能力和对学习过程的影响缺乏评估。
- **不同观点的交锋**: 支持者认为AI可以提高效率，反对者则担心其准确性和对学习效果的负面影响。

data.author: camhayes

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于如何移居欧洲并获得合法居留权的不同途径和建议，包括通过学生签证、工作签证和家庭关系等。

不同观点：
• [m_dupont] 认为通过申请大学并获得学生签证是移居国外的有效途径。他分享了自己的经历：通过申请德国大学并获得学生签证，毕业后较快找到了工作并获得了工作许可。他还提到许多国家为毕业于本国大学的外国人提供快速通道居留许可。

• [tkiolp4] 强调“移民”这一术语，指出使用这一术语并无羞耻之处，暗示应正视移居国外的法律和身份问题。

• [whatevermom] 指出申请学生签证时应针对具体国家而不是整个欧盟，因为各国使馆的程序和严格程度可能不同。同时，他表示对“蓝卡”不了解，建议具体查询目标国家的规定。

• [lipowitz] 认为如果计划在18个月内就读研究生，公司一般不会感兴趣，除非员工对公司有很大的投资价值或联系。

• [bojan] 解释了荷兰的博士研究生有薪水且是获得工作/居留签证的简便途径，但也提醒住房市场问题。他还提供了关于“知识移民签证”的相关链接。

• [michpoch] 指出不同国家和情况（如美国到欧盟国家）的移民路径可能差异很大，分享了自己通过签订瑞士工作合同并从欧盟国家迁移过去的经历。

• [elros] 询问是否想找美国雇主派往欧盟工作，暗示这是一种可能的移民途径。

• [vouaobrasil] 认为如果对研究生学习感兴趣，不应直接申请公司，而应先通过学生签证进入目标国家，在学位接近完成时再申请公司。

• [keiferski] 指出通过家庭关系或 ancestry（祖先）移民可能比研究生学习或工作更容易。

• [apwell23] 强调“移民”和“外派”的区别，指出“移民”通常是更长久的情况，而“外派”则是暂时的。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一在于移居国外时是通过学生签证途径还是直接找工作更有效。
• 讨论中多次提到具体国家之间的差异，强调针对具体国家的签证和移民政策查询的重要性。
• 对“移民”和“外派”这两个术语的定义和使用存在一定的讨论，部分评论者认为应明确区分。

• [michpoch] 指出不同国家和情况（如美国到欧盟国家）的移民路径可能差异很大，分享了自己通过签订瑞士工作合同并从欧盟国家迁移过去的经历。

• [elros] 询问是否想找美国雇主派往欧盟工作，暗示这是一种可能的移民途径。

• [vouaobrasil] 认为如果对研究生学习感兴趣，不应直接申请公司，而应先通过学生签证进入目标国家，在学位接近完成时再申请公司。

• [keiferski] 指出通过家庭关系或 ancestry（祖先）移民可能比研究生学习或工作更容易。

• [apwell23] 强调“移民”和“外派”的区别，指出“移民”通常是更长久的情况，而“外派”则是暂时的。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一在于移居国外时是通过学生签证途径还是直接找工作更有效。
• 讨论中多次提到具体国家之间的差异，强调针对具体国家的签证和移民政策查询的重要性。
• 对“移民”和“外派”这两个术语的定义和使用存在一定的讨论，部分评论者认为应明确区分。

data.title: Show HN: I made a 3D printed VTOL drone
data.author: tsungxu
data.article_summary: Tsung Xu在2025年6月10日发布文章，介绍他自制的3D打印垂直起降（VTOL）无人机，该无人机能够飞行130英里，持续飞行3小时，可能是世界上飞行距离和续航时间最长的3D打印VTOL无人机之一。Tsung在此项目之前几乎没有CAD、3D打印或空气动力学建模的经验，且仅在一个月前才开始使用3D打印机。他用了90天完成该项目，尽管视频因后期制作限制未能详细展示所有挑战和细节，但他表示如有兴趣可以提供更多设计和建造过程的信息。Tsung对该成果感到非常自豪，尤其是获得了Reid Hoffman的关注和转发。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：自制固定翼无人机 vs 使用现成商用无人机进行土地测绘任务的可行性及相关技术问题

不同观点：
• energywut：认为使用商用DJI无人机进行测绘任务时，电池续航和更换问题是个挑战，考虑是否值得追求自制固定翼无人机来完成任务。他提到地形陡峭和空域限制问题，担心固定翼无人机在转弯时无法灵活操作。
• the__alchemist：提出泡沫框架设计可能是一个不错的选择，并认为3D打印的框架在刚性上不如碳纤维，但对于固定翼无人机来说可能足够。同时指出ArduPilot的设置体验差，而商用无人机普遍使用PX4固件。
• bufferoverflow：认为该设计中垂直和水平飞行使用独立电机虽然简化了设计，但会导致飞行效率低下，因为垂直电机在水平飞行时会产生阻力。

补充讨论：
• cwmoore：引用一句话表达对自建飞行器这一成就的敬佩，认为现代工具链使得从想象到现实的转变更加便捷。
• normie3000：对项目所需的技能和知识表示兴趣，并询问ArduPilot的自定义程度以及无人机控制的独特性或标准化问题。
• ImageDeeply：赞扬这种DIY精神，鼓励其他人追求自己的兴趣，无需等待正式的许可或指导。
• georgel：询问无人机的载重能力，对额外载荷下的表现感兴趣。
• mlsu：对使用小尺寸打印机打印大尺寸机翼的连接问题表示关注，并提到在解决此问题前会继续使用泡沫板建模。
• mystraline、protocolture、asadm：对项目的材料清单（BoM）和3D打印文件（STL）表示兴趣，希望能够复现该项目。
• 3x3m3：关注无人机的遥控距离问题。

争议焦点：
• 固定翼无人机在复杂地形（陡峭和空域受限）下的适用性和灵活性问题。
• 自制无人机设计中垂直和水平飞行电机分离导致的效率问题。

I made this 130 mile capable VTOL drone in only 90 days. It can fly for 3 hours on a single charge. That would make it one of the longest range and endurance 3D printed VTOLs in the world.
This is the thing I'm most proud of building to date!
Before this project, I was a total CAD, 3D printing and aerodynamic modeling beginner. I had only
built and flown one VTOL before
. My CAD skills were restricted to extrusions of basic sketches. My Bambu A1 3D printer was only one month old, and I had never tried printing foaming PLA. I had never used any aerodynamic modeling tools to simulate lift-to-drag ratios or stability curves like Cm-alpha.
This video edit ended up shorter than I planned. Being my first Youtube video with significant post production effort, I underestimated the work required to make a longer in-depth video with voiceover, edited footage, etc.
Because of that, I did not discuss dozens of project challenges like how I chose the design parameters, learnt airframe CAD design, sourced components, improved foaming PLA print quality, in-depth power loss troubleshooting, and many more challenges this project faced.
If you want more details on my design and build process, let me know!
P.S. Reid Hoffman just
quote tweeted
my viral
video post on X
:
A century ago, you needed at least a brother and a bicycle shop to pioneer flight. Today, you just need the right toolchain…
Incredibly humbling!

data.title: Xeneva Operating System
data.author: psnehanshu
data.article_summary: XenevaOS 是一个从头构建的操作系统，支持 x86_64 和 ARM64 架构。其内核名为 "Aurora"，采用混合内核设计，整个系统称为 "Xeneva"。该系统具有多种功能，包括 ACPI 支持、x64 和 ARM64 内核、高半内存、驱动加载、SSE/SSE3、USB3、Intel 高清音频、多处理器支持等。它还包括一个名为 "Deodhai" 的合成窗口管理器，一个名为 "Chitralekha" 的图形库，以及一个支持基本 ANSI/VT100 转义序列的终端。此外，Xeneva 还提供音频服务器、网络支持以及多种应用程序和驱动。该项目欢迎开发者贡献代码、文档、错误报告和功能建议，并且主要在 Windows 环境下构建。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对XenevaOS项目的不同观点和讨论

不同观点：
• **项目团队介绍及目标**  
  - **Team Xeneva的观点**: XenevaOS是由两位开发者组成的团队项目，最初是Manas的个人爱好项目，现在已发展为针对现代计算和硬件的专业操作系统项目。目标是扩展操作系统的潜力到多个领域，如汽车、机器人、医疗科学，特别是AR/VR/XR，优先考虑用户需求而非软件依赖。
  - **einpoklum的观点**: 质疑项目的开发背景和目的，询问项目是个人爱好还是具有其他目的（如学术或商业），并提出为何要全面开发内核、低层服务、图形桌面环境和应用程序。

• **技术设计与实现细节**  
  - **namr2000的观点**: 对系统的设计提出具体问题，包括是否类似于Unix系统、是否支持libc、IPC机制的原理以及对象格式。
  - **jrapdx3的观点**: 指出项目在Windows下构建，虽然提供了详细的构建说明，但构建环境非常具体，且不支持Windows native Hyper-V。建议提供与其他操作系统的比较以吸引贡献者。
  - **vkaku的观点**: 赞赏非Unix/POSIX风格的操作系统，鼓励更多人尝试非标准实现。

• **项目独特性与社区反馈**  
  - **yyyk的观点**: 强调新操作系统需要与现有系统有明显区别，以吸引社区注意。

XenevaOS
Xeneva is an operating system for both x86_64 and ARM64  architectures, built from the ground up. The Kernel is known as
'Aurora'
with hybrid kernel design and the entire operating system is known as
'Xeneva'
.
Please visit
Build Instructions

Documentations of XenevaOS
Contributing to the project
XenevaOS is an open-source project that welcomes contributions from developers, researchers, and enthusiasts who are passionate about low level system development. Whether you're intereseted in Kernel development, driver development, low level graphics or application level features there are many ways to get involved. We encourage contibutions in the form of code, documentation, bug reports, and feature suggestions. If you're interested in contibuting, check out out
Contribution Guideline
, explore open issues, and join the discussion to help shape the project.

44240265.article_summary: XenevaOS 是一个从头构建的操作系统，支持 x86_64 和 ARM64 架构。其内核名为 "Aurora"，采用混合内核设计，整个系统称为 "Xeneva"。该系统具有多种功能，包括 ACPI 支持、x64 和 ARM64 内核、高半内存、驱动加载、SSE/SSE3、USB3、Intel 高清音频、多处理器支持等。它还包括一个名为 "Deodhai" 的合成窗口管理器，一个名为 "Chitralekha" 的图形库，以及一个支持基本 ANSI/VT100 转义序列的终端。此外，Xeneva 还提供音频服务器、网络支持以及多种应用程序和驱动。该项目欢迎开发者贡献代码、文档、错误报告和功能建议，并且主要在 Windows 环境下构建。

data.author: gnabgib

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：车辆中安装的追踪设备及其相关技术、安全和隐私问题

不同观点：
• [aggregator-ios] 认为这些追踪设备可能由大型经销商安装，而不是制造商，且可能与LoJak销售或保险追踪有关。设备通常插入OBD端口，并可能导致电动车电池的异常消耗。如果介意，可以自行移除。
• [seethishat] 指出业余无线电爱好者几十年来一直在使用APRS进行追踪，认为即使是老旧车辆也可以被追踪，带有一定的调侃意味。
• [eschneider] 提出大多数追踪设备使用运动传感器进入低功耗模式，只有在移动时才会传输信号，提醒如果要追踪需要注意这一点。
• [theoreticalmal] 表示其行业涉及IoT追踪设备，提到在非洲等地，这些设备可能被用于盗车，通过GPS干扰和无线电定位技术。
• [vv_] 认为使用RTL-SDR和LTE天线比购买专业设备更便宜，但对普通人来说，检测这些信号并不容易，因为IoT使用的频段也包含正常LTE信号。
• [goda90] 担心如果与执法人员有关系的人试图追踪，会更加容易，并提供了相关链接支持其观点。
• [userbinator] 提出使用EMP来摧毁车辆中的追踪设备，特别是对于无电子设备的机械柴油车。
• [weinzierl] 认为尝试隐藏位置数据已经不太可能，数据已经成为商品，建议不要假设可以永久隐藏。
• [Daviey] 指出相关研究未考虑到技术被犯罪分子利用的可能性，他们可以利用这些技术找到合法的追踪器并进行盗窃。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的技术包括OBD端口设备、APRS、运动传感器、EMP等。
• 隐私和安全是主要关注点，特别是设备未披露安装以及可能被犯罪利用的问题。
• 争议焦点在于如何有效检测和移除追踪设备，以及普通人是否具备相关技术能力。
• 讨论还涉及到更广泛的数据隐私问题，认为位置数据已经成为难以隐藏的商品。

data.title: Another Crack in the Chain of Trust: Uncovering (Yet Another) Secure Boot Bypass
data.author: vitplister
data.article_summary: Binarly Research团队发现了一个影响大多数支持UEFI设备的Secure Boot bypass漏洞，编号为CVE-2025-3052。该漏洞源于一个使用微软第三方UEFI证书签名的模块，攻击者可利用其内存损坏漏洞在启动过程中运行未签名代码，从而绕过Secure Boot，危害系统信任链。漏洞的根本原因是不安全处理NVRAM变量，导致任意内存写入。微软在2025年6月10日的Patch Tuesday中通过向dbx数据库添加14个新哈希来缓解此问题。Secure Boot通过验证操作系统加载器的完整性和真实性来防止此类攻击，但此漏洞使其失效，可能导致早期攻击和系统防御被破坏。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：UEFI、Secure Boot与BIOS的安全性和控制权问题

不同观点：
• **baxtr**：认为UEFI和Secure Boot在防止攻击者安装bootkits和破坏操作系统安全防御方面有优势。强调了在操作系统加载前阻止恶意代码执行的重要性。
  
• **jrm4**：对UEFI/Secure Boot相较于传统BIOS的优势表示怀疑，认为用户拥有硬件就应该有完全的控制权。同时提到对不同操作系统（如Windows和Linux）的信任问题，认为用户需要自行判断和选择信任的软件。

• **db48x**：将问题归因于NVRAM变量的不安全处理，暗示这是由于技术上的 incompetence（无能）造成的，而不是UEFI或Secure Boot概念本身的问题。

• **fsflover**：提出使用开源的替代方案——TPM与Heads（https://osresearch.net/），认为这是一个有效的解决方案，并表示这个方案对自己有效。

• **jerhewet**：简单表达了对传统BIOS的怀念，希望恢复使用BIOS，显示了对新技术的不满或不适应。

补充讨论：
- **技术安全性与用户控制权的争议**：评论中既有人关注技术上的安全性（如baxtr和fsflover），也有人强调用户对自己设备的控制权（如jrm4和jerhewet）。这反映了在技术进步与用户自由之间的张力。
- **开源解决方案**：fsflover提供的开源替代方案（TPM与Heads）显示了在技术社区中，开源工具常被视为一种透明且可信的解决方案。
- **责任归属**：db48x将问题归咎于技术处理上的 incompetence，暗示问题可能源于开发者的失误，而非技术本身的缺陷。

争议焦点：UEFI/Secure Boot是否提供了足够的安全优势，以及这些优势是否值得用户牺牲对硬件的完全控制权。

44240770.article_content:
Free scan
Book a demo
×
June 10, 2025
Another Crack in the Chain of Trust: Uncovering (Yet Another) Secure Boot Bypass
By Binarly REsearch
In this blog post, the Binarly Research team documents a Secure Boot bypass that likely impacts most devices supporting UEFI. At the center of this discovery is
CVE-2025-3052 (BRLY-2025-001)
, a memory corruption vulnerability in a module signed with Microsoftâs third-party UEFI certificate. Attackers can exploit this vulnerability to run unsigned code during the boot process, effectively bypassing Secure Boot and compromising the systemâs chain of trust. Because the attackerâs code executes before the operating system even loads, it opens the door for attackers to install bootkits and undermine OS-level security defenses.
The story behind this discovery begins with a UEFI application we found on VirusTotal, signed with Microsoftâs third-party UEFI certificate. This application has been publicly available since November 2024 when it was first submitted. However, the signature data indicates it was actually signed in October 2022, suggesting it may have been circulating for much longer.
The application is a BIOS flashing tool for devices sold by DT Research, a company specializing in rugged mobile devices. Although this module was originally developed for DT Research devices only, it can run on any device that trusts the certificate with subject "
Microsoft Corporation UEFI CA 2011
" certificate. This includes the vast majority of systems, as the same certificate is widely used to sign the Linux bootloader shim, significantly increasing the potential impact of this vulnerability.
Figure 1. The vulnerable module signed with the Microsoft UEFI CA 2011 certificate
The root cause of this bug, once again, lies in the unsafe handling of NVRAM variables. Issues involving NVRAM variables have been a persistent problem in the UEFI ecosystem,
with Binarly alone responsibly disclosing hundreds of related vulnerabilities
over the past few years. Because these bugs have been so widespread and impactful, our Binarly Transparency Platform performs multiple analyses to detect these bug classes. One of these checks looks specifically for any unsafe usage of data read from NVRAM variables, and this analysis is what automatically discovered CVE-2025-3052.
As shown in the image below, the signed application reads the content of the
IhisiParamBuffer
variable and directly uses it as a pointer for multiple memory write operations, without performing any validation or sanity checks on its value. This allows an attacker to set the
IhisiParamBuffer
variable to any arbitrary address in memory, effectively granting them an arbitrary memory write primitive.
Figure 2. The signed module blindly trusting an NVRAM variable for memory writes Â (CVE-2025-3052)
We reported this finding to CERT/CC on February 26, 2025. During our disclosure with Microsoft, it became clear that this issue wasnât limited to a single module, but it actually affected 14 different modules. For this reason, to address CVE-2025-3052, Microsoft added 14 new hashes to the Secure Boot dbx as a mitigation measure, which was delivered as part of Patch Tuesday on June 10, 2025.
Secure Boot and Microsoft Certificates
Before delving into the details of CVE-2025-3052, letâs recap what Secure Boot is and what security problems it solves. First of all, Secure Boot plays a crucial role in the chain of trust built by UEFI. It can be thought of as a bridge connecting the systemâs firmware to the operating system, carrying trust from one bank to the other. At the end of the DXE phase, with the platform initialized, the firmware is ready to boot the OS. With Secure Boot, the firmware cryptographically verifies the integrity and authenticity of the OS loader before handing over control. This check stops attackers from replacing the legitimate OS loader with a malicious component, such as a bootkit. Without Secure Boot, it is trivial for attackers to gain early execution, compromising OS defenses before the OS even has a chance to install them.
Figure 3. Summary of the UEFI Secure Boot signing and verification process
UEFI applications are signed with the private part of a signing certificate (leaf certificate on the image) that chains through one or more intermediate certificates to a trusted, root CA certificate from
db
. This is for example what happens with applications signed by Microsoft, where the private key of the certificate with subject âMicrosoft Corporation UEFI CA 2011â signs the signing/leaf certificate, whose private key is in turn used to sign the Authentocode hash of the UEFI Application.
The verification process is instead based on two signature databases:
db
and
dbx
. The
db
contains a list of trusted Authenticode hashes and root certificates:
if any Authenticode hash in the
db
matches the applicationâs Authenticode hash, the application is allowed to run
if any root certificate in the
db
successfully verifies

• **jrm4**：对UEFI/Secure Boot相较于传统BIOS的优势表示怀疑，认为用户拥有硬件就应该有完全的控制权。同时提到对不同操作系统（如Windows和Linux）的信任问题，认为用户需要自行判断和选择信任的软件。

• **db48x**：将问题归因于NVRAM变量的不安全处理，暗示这是由于技术上的 incompetence（无能）造成的，而不是UEFI或Secure Boot概念本身的问题。

• **fsflover**：提出使用开源的替代方案——TPM与Heads（https://osresearch.net/），认为这是一个有效的解决方案，并表示这个方案对自己有效。

• **jerhewet**：简单表达了对传统BIOS的怀念，希望恢复使用BIOS，显示了对新技术的不满或不适应。

补充讨论：
- **技术安全性与用户控制权的争议**：评论中既有人关注技术上的安全性（如baxtr和fsflover），也有人强调用户对自己设备的控制权（如jrm4和jerhewet）。这反映了在技术进步与用户自由之间的张力。
- **开源解决方案**：fsflover提供的开源替代方案（TPM与Heads）显示了在技术社区中，开源工具常被视为一种透明且可信的解决方案。
- **责任归属**：db48x将问题归咎于技术处理上的 incompetence，暗示问题可能源于开发者的失误，而非技术本身的缺陷。

争议焦点：UEFI/Secure Boot是否提供了足够的安全优势，以及这些优势是否值得用户牺牲对硬件的完全控制权。

data.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• [tmulc18] 认为如果页面顶部有字母表，游戏会更有趣，因为他们因为忘记字母顺序而犯了错误。
• [flipnotyk] 遇到了拼写错误的问题（"Negociate"），并指出词库可能有问题，因为字典网站无法找到该词。
• [veganjay] 对游戏表示赞赏，并分享了类似游戏的链接。
• [salamanderman] 提到使用二分查找法玩游戏，并表示与伴侣一起玩很有趣。
• [gcr] 对只有首字母高亮表示不满，认为这是一个bug。
• [jmpavlec] 对游戏自称是全球"最受欢迎的"猜测游戏表示怀疑，并询问是否会有每日一词或随机词的机制。

补充讨论：
• [radpanda] 更喜欢另一个网站（alphaguess.com）的简单界面。
• [ynac] 对游戏的匹配机制感到困惑，怀疑是否只匹配单词的前两个字母。
• [csnizik] 对游戏的创意表示赞赏，并提出了技术上的建议以解决延迟问题。
• [cardamomo] 表示游戏在接近猜中时停止响应，刷新后进度丢失，但总体上对游戏有积极评价。
• [glaucon] 报告了一个技术问题，即在使用Firefox/Windows时，输入'mountain'收到错误提示。
• [pardner] 对游戏的界面设计表示赞赏，并询问是否会考虑报告用户的猜测次数数据。
• [aqme28] 认为最佳策略是二分查找法，但实时想出最佳选择很困难。
• [sarpdag] 觉得游戏有趣，但不确定是否会再次玩。
• [layer8] 对游戏自称是全球最受欢迎的猜测游戏表示调侃。

争议焦点：
- 游戏是否应提供更多提示，如字母表（[tmulc18]）。
- 词库的准确性和拼写问题（[flipnotyk]）。
- 高亮反馈是否是bug（[gcr]）。
- 游戏自称是全球"最受欢迎的"猜测游戏的合理性（[jmpavlec], [layer8]）。

data.title: OpenAI o3-pro
data.author: mfiguiere
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GPT及相关模型的性能、价格与用户体验

不同观点：
• DanMcInerney：希望GPT5在性能上有显著提升，而不仅仅是小幅改进。虽然基准测试显示改进不大，但实际使用中感觉新一代模型在处理相同任务时表现更好。他还建议是否可以训练一个专门针对任务导向数据的模型，以进一步提升代理能力。
• chad1n：猜测OpenAI可能对o3模型进行了量化，从而降低了价格，并希望有人能对所有模型进行基准测试以检查质量是否下降。
• manmal：指出新模型的基准测试结果并不比o3好多少，并质疑是否我们已经接近性能提升的极限，进入了一个边际效益递减的阶段。
• mark_l_watson：不愿意升级到Pro账户，尽管能够负担费用，但对LLM是否是实现强大AI的最终路径持怀疑态度，担心AI发展的成本与环境影响，并提到过去的AI冬天。
• WhitneyLand：认为o3已经非常强大，甚至优于Anthropic 4和Gemini 2.5，特别是在使用工具方面。尽管成本高，但前瞻性的价值值得考虑。
• swyx：引用了一篇用户评论，显示o3 Pro提供的方案具体且有根有据，改变了团队对未来的思考方式。
• ikerino：使用o3-pro后感觉输出与普通o3差别不大，尝试输入大量上下文但效果不佳。
• nickandbro：分享了一个生成SVG图片的例子，与讨论主题关系不大。
• tiahura：讨论是否值得升级到Teams账户并支付50美元，以及与Claude Max的比较。
• ChrisArchitect：提到OpenAI将o3的价格降低了80%。
• mmsc：质疑当前过多的模型是否会让用户感到困惑，并询问最终目标是什么。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于新模型的实际性能提升是否显著，以及是否值得用户升级到更高级的账户或模型。
• 不同用户对模型的使用体验和性价比有不同看法，有些人认为高级模型的表现并不如宣传的那样突出。
• 还有人关注AI发展的长期成本与环境影响，以及对LLM是否是实现强大AI的最终路径持怀疑态度。
• 价格和模型的命名策略也是讨论的热点，用户对价格降低和不同模型的命名方式有不同的解读。

data.title: A Family of Non-Periodic Tilings, Describable Using Elementary Tools
data.author: joshu
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种使用基本工具（如模算术和向量几何）构造的非周期性铺砖方法。这些铺砖展示了一种新的结构规律性，称为模错列旋转对称。该构造独立于先前的铺砖理论，包含12张图示和13页内容，提交至组合数学领域。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：非周期性铺砖的区别与应用

不同观点：
• tocs3认为，虽然注意到这篇论文，但对内容理解可能有困难，并关注这些瓷砖与其他非周期性铺砖的区别。他表现出对具体技术细节的兴趣，但尚未深入阅读。

• jameshart则从应用角度出发，建议将这些数学产生的美学上有用的瓷砖形状引入瓷砖制造商或铺路石制造商的视野中。他强调了这些形状在实际应用中的潜力，特别是与六边形铺砖的对比。

• 0y提供了有关图5(b)中图案的来源信息，指出该图案最早由Jan Sallmann-Räder在社交媒体上发布，并提供了链接以供参考。这显示了对图案原创性和传播路径的关注。

• joshu补充了论文的全标题，并指出这些图案是Miki Imura的螺旋镶嵌。他提供了有关该研究的更多背景信息，识别出具体的研究者及其贡献。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点可能在于这些新非周期性铺砖的具体技术细节和实际应用价值。tocs3表现出对理解这些细节的兴趣，而jameshart则更关注其实际应用和美学价值。

• 0y和joshu提供了有关图案来源和研究者背景的补充信息，帮助其他讨论者更好地理解这些图案的历史和学术背景。

• 讨论还涉及到社交媒体在学术和艺术图案传播中的作用，0y提供的链接显示了社交媒体在图案传播和共享中的影响。

Abstract:
We present a construction of a family of non-periodic tilings using elementary tools such as modular arithmetic and vector geometry. These tilings exhibit a distinct type of structural regularity, which we term modulo-staggered rotational symmetry. The construction is self-contained and does not rely on previous tiling theories or systems.

data.title: Web-scraping AI bots cause disruption for scientific databases and journals
data.author: tchalla
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了网络爬虫机器人对科学数据库和期刊网站造成的干扰问题。这些自动化程序试图从网站上抓取大量内容，导致服务器过载，影响正常用户访问。特别是随着生成式人工智能（AI）工具的兴起，如聊天机器人和图像生成器，这类爬虫活动愈加猖獗。许多学术出版商和研究机构报告称，机器人流量已超过真实用户，导致服务中断和运营问题。例如，在线图像库DiscoverLife和医学期刊出版商BMJ都受到了影响。尽管开放获取的内容欢迎合理重用，但一些爬虫行为过于激进，给资源有限的组织带来了巨大压力。网站所有者正努力阻止这些机器人，但任务艰巨，亟需解决方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对大量图像数据的抓取问题及其解决方案

不同观点：
• fogx认为，可以直接提供图像数据的打包下载（dump），而不是让用户去抓取300万张图像。将文件放在CDN或Google上可以有效解决问题，简化数据获取流程。

• atonse则质疑，为什么这个问题以前没有成为搜索引擎爬虫的问题？他认为当前问题可能不是单个爬虫行为不当，而是由于存在500个爬虫同时运作导致的。

• OutOfHere提出采用工作量证明（Proof-of-Work, PoW）机制，通过要求请求中包含足够的nonce来阻止不当请求。然而，他同时指出，这种方法可能会增加能源消耗，加重电力负担。他更倾向于升级服务器，但认为这并非长久之计。

补充讨论：
• fogx的建议旨在通过简化数据获取来减少不必要的爬取行为，但并未涉及大规模数据传输可能带来的带宽和存储问题。
• atonse的观点引出了问题背后的潜在原因——多个爬虫的并发操作，而非单个爬虫的问题，这表明问题的规模和管理上的复杂性。
• OutOfHere的PoW建议提供了一种技术解决方案，但同时也意识到该方法在能源消耗上的负面影响，并提出服务器升级作为另一种不完美的选择。

争议焦点：
• 针对大规模数据抓取问题的最佳解决方案存在争议。一方主张简化下载流程，另一方则在讨论技术限制和潜在的环境影响。

44241089.article_content:
Web-scraping AI bots cause disruption for scientific databases and journals
Download PDF
Twitter
Facebook
Email
You have full access to this article via your institution.
Download PDF
Some websites have been overwhelmed by the sheer volume of bot traffic.
Credit: Marco VDM/Getty
In February, the online image repository
DiscoverLife
, which contains nearly three million photographs of different species, started to receive millions of hits to its website every day — a much higher volume than normal. At times, this spike in traffic was so high that it
slowed the site down
to the point that it became unusable. The culprit? Bots.
These automated programs, which attempt to ‘scrape’ large amounts of content from websites, are increasingly becoming a headache for scholarly publishers and researchers who run sites hosting journal papers, databases and other resources.
Open-source AI chatbots are booming — what does this mean for researchers?
Much of the bot traffic comes from anonymized IP addresses, and the sudden increase has led many website owners to suspect that these web-scrapers are gathering data to train
generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools
such as chatbots and image generators.
“It’s the wild west at the moment,” says Andrew Pitts, the chief executive of PSI, a company based in Oxford, UK, that provides a global repository of validated IP addresses for the scholarly communications community. “The biggest issue is the sheer volume of requests” to access a website, “which is causing strain on their systems. It costs money and causes disruption to genuine users.”
Those that run affected sites are working on ways to block the bots and reduce the disruption they cause. But this is no easy task, especially for organizations with limited resources. “These smaller ventures could go extinct if these sorts of issues are not dealt with,” says Michael Orr, a zoologist at the Stuttgart State Museum of Natural History in Germany.
A flood of bots
Internet bots have been around for decades, and some have been useful. For example, Google and other search engines have bots that scan millions of web pages to identify and retrieve content. But the
rise of generative AI
has led to a deluge of bots, including many ‘bad’ ones that scrape without permission.
This year, the BMJ, a publisher of medical journals based in London, has
seen bot traffic to its websites surpass that of real users
. The aggressive behaviour of these bots overloaded the publisher’s servers and led to interruptions in services for legitimate customers, says Ian Mulvany, BMJ’s chief technology officer.
Social scientists battle bots to glean insights from online chatter
Other publishers report similar issues. “We’ve seen a huge increase in what we call ‘bad bot’ traffic,” says Jes Kainth, a service delivery director based in Brighton, UK, at Highwire Press, an Internet hosting service that specializes in scholarly publications. “It’s a big problem.”
The Confederation of Open Access Repositories (COAR)
reported in April
that more than 90% of 66 members it surveyed had experienced AI bots scraping content from their sites — of which roughly two-thirds had experienced service disruptions as a result. “Repositories are open access, so in a sense, we welcome the reuse of the contents,” says Kathleen Shearer, COAR’s executive director. “But some of these bots are super aggressive, and it’s leading to service outages and significant operational problems.”
Training data
One factor driving the rise in AI bots was a revelation that came with the
release of DeepSeek
, a Chinese-built large language model (LLM). Before that, most LLMs required a huge amount of computational power to create, explains Rohit Prajapati, a development and operations manager at Highwire Press. But the developers behind DeepSeek showed that an LLM that
rivals popular generative-AI tools
could be made with many fewer resources, kick-starting an explosion of bots seeking to scrape the data needed to train this type of model.

data.author: rkaveland
data.article_summary: 这篇文章将现代互联网比作一个巨大而混乱的图书馆，用户在其中寻找有价值的内容变得愈发困难。文章描述了在图书馆中遇到咄咄逼人的管理员（比喻搜索引擎或广告服务），试图推销无用的商品（如塑料喇叭），以及发现大量看似相关、实则充斥着广告或无意义内容的钢琴书籍（比喻经过SEO优化的网页）。作者回顾了过去互联网搜索的有效性，指出如今即使明确知道所需内容，也难以通过搜索引擎找到。文章还讨论了SEO和搜索引擎之间的“猫鼠游戏”，以及 affiliate 链接的泛滥，指出这些问题可能难以根除。作者建议将搜索服务公共化，但同时也承认即便如此，人类仍可能找到方法操纵系统。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI和大语言模型（LLM）在搜索和信息获取中的应用及其经济和道德问题

不同观点：
• karel-3d 对LLM的经济可行性表示怀疑，认为投入的巨额资金意味着公司将需要通过用户支付或广告获取巨大收益，但目前作为用户可以享受免费服务是一个不错的"免费午餐"。
• willvarfar 提出一个理想化的解决方案，建议欧盟创建一个公共知识机构，结合图书馆和科技，推动公共利益的搜索引擎和AI发展，以避免商业化偏见。
• boothby 担心广告商很快会将产品植入训练数据中，从而影响LLM的中立性和搜索结果的公正性。
• GnarfGnarf 质疑我们是否有权期望免费搜索服务，并询问用户愿意为无广告搜索支付多少费用，认为"免费时代"是在为未来的收费做准备。
• elif 支持 boothby 的观点，通过个人经历说明当前搜索引擎被广告主导，导致用户体验不佳。
• WiggleGuy 创建了一个多搜索引擎查询工具，认为虽然有更好的搜索方式，但非技术用户很少使用，导致主流搜索引擎仍占主导地位。
• Peteragain 提出一个解决方案，建议将数据公开，允许自由市场开发用户界面和过滤器，类似于道路由国家管理，车辆由市场销售的模式。
• pajamasam 注意到AI生成的内容网站激增，但并不总是以广告为目的，质疑这些内容是否旨在推动用户使用LLM。
• BrenBarn 认为AI被广告充斥是不可避免的，除非社会决定拒绝这种趋势，并指出问题的根源在于社会经济系统的不平等。
• Kiyo-Lynn 希望搜索引擎更像公共图书馆，专注于提供信息而不是商业推荐。
• gerdesj 对LLM用于搜索持怀疑态度，认为LLM由于其预测下一个标记的性质，无法保证事实的准确性，且对时事无能为力。
• ChrisMarshallNY 对公共机构的腐败问题提出警告，认为即使AI也难以避免。
• hug 推荐Kagi作为一种更好的搜索工具，认为其结合LLM聊天界面的高级计划提供了更好的用户体验。
• iamkeithmccoy 预测AI迟早会被广告充斥，失去其当前的优势。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于AI和大语言模型是否会被商业利益驱动，导致搜索结果的公正性和中立性受到影响。
• 部分用户对当前搜索引擎的广告泛滥和SEO垃圾内容感到不满，希望有更公正和专注于信息的替代方案。
• 一些评论者提出了理想化的解决方案，如公共知识机构和数据公开，以减少商业化影响，但也有评论者对这些方案的实际可行性和潜在腐败问题表示担忧。
• 对LLM技术本身的信任问题也被提及，特别是其在事实准确性和时事上的局限性。
